327	    """Visible-area capture of the session's active window's active pane.
328	
329	    Returns (text, skipped). `skipped=True` when the target pane is the one
330	    running this script — capturing it would include `tsum`'s own output
331	    (the prompt, the previous summary if any), which pollutes the LLM input
332	    and produces a recursive-looking session description.
333	
334	    Capture window is sized to the pane's actual height, clamped to
335	    [_DEEP_MIN_LINES, _DEEP_MAX_LINES]. Smaller than ~20 lines is usually
336	    useless; larger than ~100 dominates the prompt and risks leaking lots
337	    of scrollback content.
338	    """
339	    active = next((w for w in wins if w.active), wins[0] if wins else None)
340	    if active is None:
341	        return "", False
342	    target = f"{session}:{active.index}"
343	
344	    # Self-capture guard. `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}'` returns
345	    # the active pane of the target; compare against $TMUX_PANE.
346	    if my_pane:
347	        target_pane = _tmux(
348	            "display-message", "-p", "-t", target, "#{pane_id}"
349	        ).strip()
350	        if target_pane and target_pane == my_pane:
351	            return "", True
352	
353	    # Size the capture to the pane's actual visible height.
354	    height_str = _tmux(
355	        "display-message", "-p", "-t", target, "#{pane_height}"
356	    ).strip()
357	    try:
358	        height = int(height_str)
359	    except ValueError:
360	        height = 40  # reasonable fallback
361	    lines = max(_DEEP_MIN_LINES, min(height, _DEEP_MAX_LINES))
362	
363	    text = _tmux(
364	        "capture-pane", "-p", "-S", f"-{lines}", "-t", target
365	    ).rstrip()
366	    return text, False
367	
368	
369	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
370	# Cache (keyed by full-prompt hash)
371	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
372	def cache_path(deep: bool) -> Path:
373	    """Per-host, per-mode cache file. Splitting deep / shallow into two slots
374	    means toggling --deep / --shallow doesn't overwrite the other mode's
375	    latest cached summary — each can be served independently when its own
376	    prompt-hash hits.
377	    """
378	    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME") or os.path.expanduser("~/.cache")
379	    d = Path(base) / "tmux-session-summary"
380	    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
381	    host = socket.gethostname().split(".")[0] or "host"
382	    mode = "deep" if deep else "shallow"
383	    return d / f"{host}-{mode}.json"
384	
385	
386	# Bump when the cache schema changes. Mismatched-version files are silently
387	# ignored and overwritten on next refresh.
388	#   v2 → v3: structure signature renamed to full-prompt hash (`sig` →
389	#            `prompt_hash`); `ttl_seconds` dropped (no longer meaningful
390	#            under hash-based invalidation).
391	_CACHE_VERSION = "v3"
392	
393	
394	def lookup_cache(prompt_hash: str, deep: bool) -> tuple[list[dict] | None, str]:
395	    """Return (summaries, reason) where reason ∈ {"hit", "throttled", "miss"}.
396	
397	    - "hit":       cached prompt_hash matches → identical LLM input,
398	                   identical answer, reuse regardless of age.
399	    - "throttled": prompt_hash differs but the cache is younger than
400	                   TSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL → reuse stale summary to
401	                   absorb high-frequency churn (htop/watch/progress bars).
402	    - "miss":      stale and out-of-throttle, or no cache at all → caller
403	                   should hit the LLM.
404	    """
405	    p = cache_path(deep)
406	    if not p.is_file():
407	        return None, "miss"
408	    try:
409	        data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
410	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
411	        return None, "miss"
412	    if data.get("version") != _CACHE_VERSION:
413	        return None, "miss"
414	    summaries = data.get("sessions")
415	    if not isinstance(summaries, list):
416	        return None, "miss"
417	
418	    if data.get("prompt_hash") == prompt_hash:
419	        return summaries, "hit"
420	
421	    age = time.time() - float(data.get("generated_at_epoch", 0))
422	    if age < TSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL:
423	        return summaries, "throttled"
424	
425	    return None, "miss"
426	
427	
428	def save_cache(prompt_hash: str, summaries: list[dict], deep: bool) -> None:
429	    p = cache_path(deep)
430	    try:
431	        p.write_text(
432	            json.dumps(
433	                {
434	                    "version": _CACHE_VERSION,
435	                    "prompt_hash": prompt_hash,
436	                    "generated_at_epoch": time.time(),
437	                    "sessions": summaries,
438	                },
439	                indent=2,
440	            ),
441	            encoding="utf-8",
442	        )
443	    except OSError as e:
444	        err.print(f"[yellow]tmux-session-summary: cache write failed: {e}[/yellow]")
445	
446	
447	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
448	# Prompt construction
449	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
450	PROMPT_PREAMBLE = """\
451	You are summarizing a developer's tmux sessions so they can quickly remember \
452	what each one is for, AND decide which sessions are safe to close. The data \
453	below is from `tmux list-sessions` + `tmux list-windows`. The user has many \
454	cryptically-named sessions (numbers, dates, project slugs) and wants a \
455	one-glance refresher + a clear closability rating.
456	
457	For EACH session, infer:
458	  - A concise one-line summary (<= 70 chars) describing what the user is \
459	doing there. Be specific: name the project, the running task, the file being \
460	edited. Avoid generic phrases like "a session" or "various work".
461	  - 1-3 "important_windows": the editor window, the long-running process, \
462	the primary terminal — whichever stand out as load-bearing. Skip if nothing \
463	really stands out.
464	  - A "closability" rating — how safe it is to close this session RIGHT NOW \
465	without losing work:
466	      "safe"   → nothing important; close freely. Only idle shells \
467	(zsh/bash/fish), lazygit browsers, monitoring (tail -f, htop, watch), or \
468	detached sessions with last_attached >7 days ago and no running process.
469	      "check"  → might lose work; review before closing. Editor open with a \
470	filename (might have unsaved buffer), attached but currently idle, recent \
471	activity, unclear state.
472	      "keep"   → active in-progress work; do NOT close. Coding-agent CLI \
473	running (claude/opencode/codex/aider/gemini), long-running process \
474	(python/node/npm run dev/cargo run/docker compose up/pytest), \
475	attached + currently editing, --deep output showing a build/test running.
476	  - A one-line "closability_reason" (<= 50 chars) explaining the rating.
477	
478	When in doubt, pick "check" rather than "safe" — false safe is worse than \
479	false check.
480	
481	Summary heuristics:
482	  - `nvim`, `vim`, `code` → likely an editor; the filename in cmd matters.
483	  - `python`, `node`, `npm`, `cargo`, `make`, `pytest`, `docker` → likely a \
484	running build/server/test. Note it.
485	  - `zsh`, `bash`, `fish` alone → idle shell; usually NOT important.
486	  - `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `aider` → coding agent session.
487	  - Same cwd across many windows → that cwd is the project root.
488	  - `wt` / `worktree` / `tries/` / `coding-agent/` in session name → git \
489	worktree experiment, often short-lived.
490	
491	Respond with STRICT JSON only, no prose, no code fences:
492	[
493	  {
494	    "session": "<name>",
495	    "summary": "<<=70 chars>",
496	    "closability": "safe" | "check" | "keep",
497	    "closability_reason": "<<=50 chars>",
498	    "important_windows": [
499	      {"index": <int>, "name": "<window_name>", "why": "<<=40 chars>"}
500	    ]
501	  }
502	]
503	"""
504	
505	
506	def build_prompt(sessions: list[Session], deep: bool) -> str:
507	    parts = [PROMPT_PREAMBLE, "", "--- SESSIONS ---", ""]
508	    for s in sessions:
509	        attached_marker = "(attached)" if s.attached else ""
510	        parts.append(f"session: {s.name} [{len(s.windows)} windows] {attached_marker}".rstrip())
511	        for w in s.windows:
512	            active = " ACTIVE" if w.active else ""
513	            pane_note = f" ({w.panes} panes)" if w.panes > 1 else ""
514	            parts.append(f"  {w.index}: {w.name:<14} {w.cwd}    {w.cmd}{pane_note}{active}")
515	        if deep:
516	            if s.active_pane_skipped:
517	                parts.append(
518	                    "  (skipped active-pane capture: this is the pane running tsum)"
519	                )
520	            elif s.active_pane_tail:
521	                tail_lines = s.active_pane_tail.splitlines()
522	                parts.append(
523	                    f"  recent output (visible area, {len(tail_lines)} lines, active pane):"
524	                )
525	                for line in tail_lines:
526	                    # Per-line clip so a pathological line doesn't blow tokens.
527	                    parts.append(f"    {line[:200]}")
528	        parts.append("")
529	    parts.append("Return JSON now.")
530	    return "\n".join(parts)
531	
532	
533	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
534	# Agent invocation
535	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
536	def detect_agent() -> str | None:
537	    """Pick an agent: explicit override > priority list from SSOT.
538	
539	    Priority list is `$AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY` from
540	    dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh. Override globally by exporting that
541	    var; override per-call by setting AICAP_AGENT.
542	    """
543	    if AICAP_AGENT:
544	        if AICAP_AGENT == "http" or shutil.which(AICAP_AGENT):
545	            return AICAP_AGENT
546	        err.print(
547	            f"[red]AICAP_AGENT={AICAP_AGENT!r} but that CLI isn't on PATH.[/red]"
548	        )
549	        return None
550	    for cand in AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY:
551	        if shutil.which(cand):
552	            return cand
553	    return None
554	
555	
556	def model_for(agent: str) -> str:
557	    return {
558	        "claude": AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL or "(default)",
559	        "opencode": AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL or "(default)",
560	        "codex": AICAP_CODEX_MODEL or "(default)",
561	        "cursor-agent": AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL or "(default)",
562	        "http": AICAP_HTTP_MODEL,
563	    }.get(agent, "?")
564	
565	
566	def invoke_agent(agent: str, prompt: str, timeout: float) -> str:
567	    """Run the agent in one-shot mode and return raw reply text.
568	
569	    Returns empty string on failure (caller falls back to metadata-only
570	    rendering).
571	    """
572	    if agent == "http":
573	        return _invoke_http(prompt, timeout)
574	    base = AGENT_CONFIG[agent]["base"]
575	    try:
576	        result = subprocess.run(
577	            [*base, prompt],
578	            capture_output=True,
579	            text=True,
580	            timeout=timeout,
581	        )
582	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
583	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} timed out after {timeout:.0f}s[/red]")
584	        return ""
585	    except FileNotFoundError:
586	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} not on PATH (race vs detect_agent)[/red]")
587	        return ""
588	    if result.returncode != 0:
589	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
590	        if result.stderr.strip():
591	            err.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr.strip()[:500]}[/dim]")
592	        return ""
593	    return result.stdout
594	
595	
596	def _invoke_http(prompt: str, timeout: float) -> str:
597	    payload = json.dumps({
598	        "model": AICAP_HTTP_MODEL,
599	        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
600	        "stream": False,
601	    }).encode("utf-8")
602	    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
603	    if AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:
604	        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY}"
605	    req = urllib.request.Request(AICAP_HTTP_URL, data=payload, headers=headers, method="POST")
606	    try:
607	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
608	            body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
609	    except (urllib.error.HTTPError, urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as e:
610	        err.print(f"[red]http: {e}[/red]")
611	        return ""
612	    try:
613	        parsed = json.loads(body)
614	        return parsed["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
615	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
616	        err.print(f"[red]http: unexpected response shape[/red] [dim]{body[:300]}[/dim]")
617	        return ""
618	
619	
620	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
621	# Response parsing
622	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
623	_CLOSABILITY_TIERS = ("safe", "check", "keep")
624	
625	
626	def parse_reply(reply: str) -> list[dict] | None:
627	    """Extract the JSON array of session summaries from the agent's reply.
628	
629	    Agents sometimes wrap JSON in ``` fences or add a preamble despite
630	    instructions. We tolerate that by finding the first `[` and last `]`.
631	    """
632	    if not reply.strip():
633	        return None
634	    # Strip code fences if present.
635	    stripped = reply.strip()
636	    if stripped.startswith("```"):
637	        stripped = stripped.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in stripped else stripped
638	        if stripped.endswith("```"):
639	            stripped = stripped.rsplit("```", 1)[0]
640	        stripped = stripped.strip()
641	    # Find outer JSON array.
642	    start = stripped.find("[")
643	    end = stripped.rfind("]")
644	    if start == -1 or end == -1 or end < start:
645	        return None
646	    try:
647	        parsed = json.loads(stripped[start : end + 1])
648	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
649	        return None
650	    if not isinstance(parsed, list):
651	        return None
652	    # Coerce minimal shape.
653	    out: list[dict] = []
654	    for item in parsed:
655	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
656	            continue
657	        sess = str(item.get("session", "")).strip()
658	        if not sess:
659	            continue
660	        raw_closability = str(item.get("closability", "")).strip().lower()
661	        # Unknown / missing → "check" (conservative middle): per the prompt
662	        # rule "when in doubt, pick check rather than safe."
663	        closability = raw_closability if raw_closability in _CLOSABILITY_TIERS else "check"
664	        out.append({
665	            "session": sess,
666	            "summary": str(item.get("summary", "")).strip()[:140],
667	            "closability": closability,
668	            "closability_reason": str(item.get("closability_reason", "")).strip()[:80],
669	            "important_windows": [
670	                {
671	                    "index": int(w.get("index", 0)) if str(w.get("index", "")).lstrip("-").isdigit() else 0,
672	                    "name": str(w.get("name", "")).strip()[:30],
673	                    "why": str(w.get("why", "")).strip()[:80],
674	                }
675	                for w in (item.get("important_windows") or [])
676	                if isinstance(w, dict)
677	            ][:3],
678	        })
679	    return out
680	
681	
682	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
683	# Rendering
684	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
685	def _summary_by_session(summaries: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:
686	    return {s["session"]: s for s in summaries}
687	
688	
689	# Visual mapping for the three closability tiers. The glyph is plain Unicode
690	# so it survives no-color terminals; the colour is rich-styled in TTYs.
691	_TIER_GLYPHS = {"safe": "🟢", "check": "🟡", "keep": "🔴"}
692	_TIER_COLORS = {"safe": "green", "check": "yellow", "keep": "red"}
693	_TIER_FALLBACK_GLYPH = "⚪"  # used when LLM output is missing (fallback renderers)
694	
695	
696	def render_list(sessions: list[Session], summaries: list[dict], use_color: bool) -> None:
697	    """Human-readable: one block per session to stdout."""
698	    out = Console(force_terminal=use_color, no_color=not use_color, soft_wrap=True)
699	    by_name = _summary_by_session(summaries)
700	    name_width = max((len(s.name) for s in sessions), default=4)
701	    for s in sessions:
702	        info = by_name.get(s.name, {})
703	        summary = info.get("summary") or "(no summary)"
704	        tier = info.get("closability", "check")
705	        glyph = _TIER_GLYPHS.get(tier, _TIER_FALLBACK_GLYPH)
706	        color = _TIER_COLORS.get(tier, "cyan")
707	        attached = " *" if s.attached else "  "
708	        line = Text()
709	        line.append(f"{glyph} ", style="bold")
710	        # Underline the name when "keep" so the row pops even on glyph-blind terminals.
711	        name_style = f"bold {color}"
712	        if tier == "keep":
713	            name_style += " underline"
714	        line.append(f"{s.name:<{name_width}}{attached} ", style=name_style)
715	        line.append(f"[{len(s.windows):>2}w] ", style="dim")
716	        line.append(summary, style="white")
717	        reason = info.get("closability_reason", "")
718	        if reason:
719	            line.append(f"  ({reason})", style="dim italic")
720	        out.print(line)
721	        for w_info in info.get("important_windows", []):
722	            why = f"  — {w_info['why']}" if w_info.get("why") else ""
723	            idx = w_info.get("index", 0)
724	            wname = w_info.get("name", "")
725	            sub = Text()
726	            sub.append("    └ ", style="dim")
727	            sub.append(f"w{idx}: {wname}", style="green")
728	            sub.append(why, style="dim")
729	            out.print(sub)
730	
731	
732	def render_picker(sessions: list[Session], summaries: list[dict]) -> None:
733	    """TSV `<session>\\t<one-line>` for fzf consumption.
734	
735	    Always plain text (no ANSI), always stdout. fzf will display the second
736	    column via --with-nth=2.
737	    """
738	    by_name = _summary_by_session(summaries)
739	    for s in sessions:
740	        info = by_name.get(s.name, {})
741	        summary = info.get("summary") or "(no summary)"
742	        tier = info.get("closability", "check")
743	        glyph = _TIER_GLYPHS.get(tier, _TIER_FALLBACK_GLYPH)
744	        attached = "*" if s.attached else " "
745	        win_count = f"[{len(s.windows):>2}w]"
746	        print(f"{s.name}\t{glyph} {attached} {win_count} {summary}")
747	
748	
749	def render_fallback_list(sessions: list[Session], use_color: bool) -> None:
750	    """Used when the LLM failed: print bare metadata so the user still sees something."""
751	    out = Console(force_terminal=use_color, no_color=not use_color, soft_wrap=True)
752	    name_width = max((len(s.name) for s in sessions), default=4)
753	    for s in sessions:
754	        attached = " *" if s.attached else "  "
755	        line = Text()
756	        line.append(f"{_TIER_FALLBACK_GLYPH} ", style="bold")
757	        line.append(f"{s.name:<{name_width}}{attached} ", style="bold cyan")
758	        line.append(f"[{len(s.windows):>2}w] ", style="dim")
759	        # Best-effort tag: most-common cwd basename + active window's cmd
760	        cwds = [w.cwd for w in s.windows]
761	        common = max(set(cwds), key=cwds.count) if cwds else ""
762	        basename = os.path.basename(common.rstrip("/")) or common
763	        active = next((w for w in s.windows if w.active), None)
764	        active_str = f" — {active.cmd}" if active else ""
765	        line.append(f"{basename}{active_str}", style="white")
766	        out.print(line)
767	
768	
769	def render_fallback_picker(sessions: list[Session]) -> None:
770	    """Picker fallback when LLM failed."""
771	    for s in sessions:
772	        attached = "*" if s.attached else " "
773	        cwds = [w.cwd for w in s.windows]
774	        common = max(set(cwds), key=cwds.count) if cwds else ""
775	        basename = os.path.basename(common.rstrip("/")) or common
776	        active = next((w for w in s.windows if w.active), None)
777	        active_str = f" — {active.cmd}" if active else ""
778	        print(f"{s.name}\t{_TIER_FALLBACK_GLYPH} {attached} [{len(s.windows):>2}w] {basename}{active_str}")
779	
780	
781	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
782	# CLI
783	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
784	def _env_truthy(val: str) -> bool:
785	    return val.strip().lower() not in ("", "0", "false", "no", "off")
786	
787	
788	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
789	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
790	        prog="tmux-session-summary",
791	        description="AI-powered overview of every tmux session.",
792	    )
793	    p.add_argument("mode", nargs="?", default="list", choices=["list", "picker"])
794	    # --deep and --shallow are mutually-resolved later (--deep wins). default
795	    # is None so we can tell "user did not pass either flag" apart from
796	    # "user explicitly chose shallow" and consult TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT only in
797	    # the former case.
798	    p.add_argument(
799	        "-d", "--deep",
800	        dest="deep", action="store_true", default=None,
801	        help="Include visible area of each session's active pane (overrides TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=0).",
802	    )
803	    p.add_argument(
804	        "--shallow",
805	        dest="deep", action="store_false",
806	        help="Force metadata-only (overrides TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1).",
807	    )
808	    p.add_argument("-r", "--refresh", action="store_true", help="Bypass cache.")
809	    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Print the prompt that would be sent; no API call.")
810	    p.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Don't read or write the cache.")
811	    p.add_argument(
812	        "--sort", choices=["alpha", "closability"], default="alpha",
813	        help="Order sessions: alpha (tmux's natural order) or closability (keep→check→safe).",
814	    )
815	    p.add_argument(
816	        "--only", choices=_CLOSABILITY_TIERS, default=None,
817	        help="Filter to one closability tier.",
818	    )
819	    args = p.parse_args()
820	    # Three-state resolution: flag explicit > env var > False.
821	    if args.deep is None:
822	        args.deep = _env_truthy(os.environ.get("TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT", ""))
823	    return args
824	
825	
826	def main() -> int:
827	    args = parse_args()
828	
829	    sessions = collect_sessions(deep=args.deep)
830	    if not sessions:
831	        resolved = shutil.which(TSUM_TMUX_BIN) or TSUM_TMUX_BIN
832	        err.print(
833	            f"[red]tmux-session-summary: no tmux sessions found via "
834	            f"{TSUM_TMUX_BIN!r} ({resolved}).[/red]"
835	        )
836	        if _LAST_TMUX_STDERR:
837	            err.print(f"[dim]tmux stderr: {_LAST_TMUX_STDERR}[/dim]")
838	        err.print(
839	            "[yellow]Possible causes:[/yellow]\n"
840	            "  - server not running → start a session first.\n"
841	            "  - multiple tmux binaries on PATH (apt vs appimage vs brew) and the\n"
842	            "    one we resolved talks a different protocol than the running server.\n"
843	            "    Fix: [cyan]export TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/path/to/correct-tmux[/cyan]\n"
844	            "    (e.g. [cyan]/bin/tmux[/cyan] if your sessions live there)."
845	        )
846	        return 1
847

906	def _render_fallback(sessions: list[Session], args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
907	    """Fallback render path — used when the LLM is unavailable or unparseable.
908

    We follow the log file with `tail -f` and stop when either:

    server-side by `ls -t … | head -1`.
    """
    if host.local:
        # Local: just `tail -F` the local cache file. Resolve `run_id` to
        # newest if empty. No SSH needed, no sentinel polling needed
        # (subprocess will exit when we Ctrl+C).
        if not run_id:
            try:
                logs = sorted(
                    LOCAL_LOG_DIR.glob("*.log"),
                    key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
                    reverse=True,
                )
                if not logs:
                    console.print(
                        f"[red]✗[/] no local fleet-apply log in {LOCAL_LOG_DIR}"
                    )
                    return 3
                run_id = logs[0].stem
            except OSError as e:
                console.print(f"[red]✗[/] read {LOCAL_LOG_DIR}: {e}")
                return 3
        log_file = LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{run_id}.log"
        exit_file = LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{run_id}.exit"
        if not log_file.exists():
            console.print(f"[red]✗[/] not found: {log_file}")
            return 3
        console.print(
            f"[dim]fleet-tail (local): following {log_file} "
            f"(Ctrl+C stops viewer; local run continues if active)[/]"
        )
        # Use plain `tail -F` and poll the sentinel from a sibling task.
        try:

            async def _local_follow() -> int:

                    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                    stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,

                        # `[role : task]` brackets as malformed tags.
                        # Use the `style=` kwarg for dim instead of inline
                        # `[dim]...[/]` markup which would be disabled.
                        console.print(
                            text,
                            markup=False,
                            highlight=False,
                            style="dim" if is_err else None,
                        )

                    while True:
                        if exit_file.exists():
                            await asyncio.sleep(1)  # let tail flush
                            proc.terminate()
                            try:
                                rc = exit_file.read_text().strip()
                            except OSError:
                                rc = "?"
                            console.print(
                                f"\n[dim]fleet-tail: local run {run_id} "
                                f"finished, rc={rc}[/]"
                            )
                            return
                        await asyncio.sleep(2)

                await asyncio.gather(
                    _drain(proc.stdout, False),
                    _drain(proc.stderr, True),
                    _watch_sentinel(),
                    return_exceptions=True,
                )
                return 0

            return asyncio.run(_local_follow())
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            console.print(
                "\n[yellow]fleet-tail: viewer interrupted; "
                "local run (if active) continues.[/]"
            )
            return 130

    # Resolve `run_id` on the remote so the user can pass `""` to mean
    # "newest". Then `tail -F` (follow + retry) on the picked log, and a
    # parallel poll loop watches for the .exit sentinel — when it appears
    # we print the exit code and break out, killing tail.
    remote_cmd = (
        "_dir=\"$HOME/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs\"; "
        f"_run={shlex.quote(run_id)}; "
        "if [ -z \"$_run\" ]; then "
        "  _run=$(ls -t \"$_dir\"/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xargs -I{} basename {} .log); "
```

### 4. **`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`** — Mental Model & Invariants

**Key tenets** (lines 1–40):
- TL;DR: `just fleet-apply` runs `chezmoi update --init` on all hosts in parallel, with optional sudo password injection from plain/prompt/Bitwarden, logs to `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC>/<host>.log`, exits with # of failed hosts
- **Pre-flight mandatory**: run `just fleet-status` before `fleet-apply` (read-only probe predicts outcome)
- Three sub-operations under `chezmoi update --init`: `git pull` → `chezmoi init` (re-render TOML, new prompts fail non-interactively) → `chezmoi apply` + run_* scripts

**Readiness probe state matrix** (lines 103–124):
- `up-to-date` ✓: no action needed
- `ready-to-update` ↻: source behind origin; safe to pull+apply
- `behind` →: same but coexists with other notes
- `drift` ⚠: remote file hand-edited; `--keep-going` skips it; use `--force` to overwrite or migrate to *.local
- `dirty` ⚠: remote source dir has uncommitted edits
- `ahead` ?: local commits on remote not on origin
- `busy` ⏳: chezmoi/ansible still running
- `init-in-progress` ⏳: chezmoi update/init mid-flight (paused at prompt elsewhere)
- `toml-mismatch` !: NEW prompt keys in template but missing from remote saved config — the "david_ubuntu" failure mode
- `not-init` ✗: ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml missing
- `no-source` ✗: chezmoi source-path invalid
- `no-chezmoi` ✗: chezmoi binary not found
- `unreachable` ✗: SSH failed

**Counter-intuitive defaults** (not explicitly called out but implied):
- `password_source` is NOT for SSH login auth (line 8–13); only for sudo
- `--keep-going` default is ON (line 1202–1216): skips drift files, continues applying rest
- First run can timeout at 7200s default (line 1104–1121) because Linuxbrew+ansible+casks are slow; steady-state is 1–5 min
- `--force` is destructive (silently overwrites hand-edits); only use if repo is source of truth (line 1189–1201)

---

### 5. **Shell Aliases / Functions**

No fleet-specific aliases found in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`. Fleet is invoked via `just fleet-*` recipes only.

---

**Summary**: Fleet is a fully-async orchestrator (`asyncssh` + `tyro` + `rich`) dispatching `chezmoi update --init` across a flat host inventory, with sophisticated password injection (plain/prompt/Bitwarden), drift detection (regex on "could not open TTY" errors), and process cleanup (bash trap + SIGHUP propagation). The mental model is "readiness probe first, then apply," with 14 distinct subcommands handling apply/diff/status/kill/tail/compact workflows.

**Source → Target mapping** (via chezmoi naming convention):

`~/bin` is added first, followed by `~/.local/bin` for auto-installed tools (uv, npm, cargo, mise).

**`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`** (.chezmoiignore.tmpl:115):
- `.local/` is **ignored entirely** — dynamically managed by package managers, not chezmoi-tracked.
- No conditional ignoring of `bin/`; it deploys on all machines.

### 3. `~/.local/bin` Usage

**Not chezmoi-managed** (except for the documented-but-apparently-missing `dot_local/bin/`):
- `mise` self-installs to `~/.local/bin/mise` (checked at shell init in `dot_config/shell/05_mise.sh:5`)

- `cargo install` → `~/.cargo/bin/` (not `~/.local/bin`)
- `.local/` directory itself is in `.chezmoiignore` (line 115) so runtime-installed content there never syncs back into the repo.

### 4. Alternative Hidden Locations

**No precedent for chezmoi-managed binaries in hidden locations**, but relevant precedents exist:
- **Agent skills**: `~/.agents/skills/` (global, npm-managed) and `.agents/skills/` (project-scope). In `.chezmoiignore` (lines 62–66) because they're owned by `npx skills` CLI and auto-restored by `run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl` when the lock file changes.
- **Private structures exist**: `private_dot_specstory/`, `private_Library/` (for macOS application dirs) — these use the `private_` prefix to enforce 0600/0700 permissions, not for organizational separation.
- **No `private_bin/` or `dot_bin/` precedent** in this repo.

### 5. Chezmoi Naming Convention

**Source → Target mapping** (`chezmoi-prefixes.md`, case examples):
- `dot_` prefix: `dot_foo` → `.foo` (keeps dotfiles visible in git)
- `executable_` prefix: adds +x bit on apply

70	                                old summary if the previous LLM call was
71	                                within this window (protects against high-
72	                                volatility deep-mode panes like htop/watch).
73	                                Identical prompts always hit, regardless of
74	                                age. Set to 0 to disable throttling.
75	                                TSUM_CACHE_TTL accepted as fallback alias.
76	    TSUM_TIMEOUT                seconds, default 60
77	    TSUM_TMUX_BIN               full path to tmux binary, default "tmux" (use this
78	                                when multiple tmux binaries are on PATH and the
79	                                server you care about runs from a specific one,
80	                                e.g. TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/bin/tmux)
81	
82	CACHE
83	    $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/<hostname>-<mode>.json
84	    (cache key is sha256(build_prompt)[:16] — identical prompts hit forever;
85	     differing prompts trigger a fresh LLM call unless throttled by
86	     TSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL)
87	EOF
88	                return 0
89	                ;;
90	            *)
91	                # Quote each forwarded arg with single quotes; embedded single
92	                # quotes get the '\'' dance so eval-time re-parsing is exact.
93	                _tsum_forward="$_tsum_forward '$(printf %s "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")'"
94	                ;;
95	        esac
96	        shift
97	    done
98	
99	    if [ "$_tsum_interactive" -eq 0 ]; then
100	        # Plain mode — let the script render to stdout/stderr directly.
101	        eval "\"\$_tsum_script\" $_tsum_forward"
102	        return $?
103	    fi
104	
105	    # Interactive: picker | fzf, switch on Enter.
106	    if ! command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
107	        printf 'tsum: -i needs fzf on PATH; falling back to plain output.\n' >&2
108	        eval "\"\$_tsum_script\" $_tsum_forward"
109	        return $?
110	    fi
111	
112	    # Force `picker` mode regardless of what got forwarded (silently strip
113	    # `list`/`picker` from the forwarded args by re-running with picker as
114	    # the explicit first arg).
115	    _tsum_selected=$(
116	        eval "\"\$_tsum_script\" picker $_tsum_forward" \
117	            | fzf --ansi \
118	                  --delimiter='	' \
119	                  --with-nth=2 \
120	                  --preview='printf "%s\n" {2}' \
121	                  --preview-window='down:3:wrap' \
122	                  --prompt='session> ' \
123	                  --header='Enter: switch  /  Esc: cancel' \
124	                  --no-multi
125	    )
126	
127	    [ -z "$_tsum_selected" ] && return 0
128	
129	    # First TAB-delimited field is the session name.
130	    _tsum_target="${_tsum_selected%%	*}"
131	
132	    # Honour TSUM_TMUX_BIN — see dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py
133	    # for the version-mismatch rationale. switch-client / attach-session MUST
134	    # use the same binary that owns the running server.
135	    _tsum_tmux_bin="${TSUM_TMUX_BIN:-tmux}"
136	    if [ -z "${TMUX:-}" ]; then
137	        # Outside tmux: attach to the chosen session instead of switch-client.
138	        "$_tsum_tmux_bin" attach-session -t "$_tsum_target"
139	    else
140	        "$_tsum_tmux_bin" switch-client -t "$_tsum_target"
141	    fi
142	}

- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.

```text
# Fleet apply — multi-host `chezmoi update` orchestrator

> **TL;DR** — `just fleet-apply` runs `chezmoi update --init` on every host
> listed in `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`, in parallel, with optional sudo
> password injection sourced from plaintext / interactive prompt / Bitwarden
> CLI. Per-host logs land under `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log`
> and the process exits with the number of failed hosts (capped at 125).
>
> **Before applying, run [`just fleet-status`](#readiness-probe-just-fleet-status)** — a read-only pre-flight probe that predicts what `fleet-apply` would do per host (up-to-date / behind / drift / busy / toml-mismatch / not-init / unreachable / ...).

Implementation: [`scripts/fleet_apply.py`](../../scripts/fleet_apply.py)
(uv inline-script: `asyncssh` + `tyro` + `rich`).

See also: [fleet-apply-vs-fabric.md](fleet-apply-vs-fabric.md) for an
archaeological comparison against the author's 2018-era Fabric `fabfile.py`
on RaspPi-Cluster — same problem shape, ~7 years of operational lessons
encoded into the current implementation.

## The fleet-* command family at a glance

The fleet- recipes split into **three layers** of concern. Pick the right one based on what you want to do:

| Recipe | What it does | Side effects | When to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `just fleet-edit` | Open `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` in `$EDITOR` (seeds an empty template on first run) | Edits inventory file only | First-time setup, adding/removing hosts |
| `just fleet-status` | **Pre-flight readiness probe** — predicts what `fleet-apply` would do per host | None (read-only, ~1.5s/host) | **Before** `fleet-apply`, to triage which hosts need attention |
| `just fleet-status-quick` | Same as `fleet-status` but skips remote `git fetch` (~0.5s/host) | None | Offline / quick re-check |
| `just fleet-apply-dry-run` | Run `chezmoi diff` on every host (full template render comparison) | Reads remote source dir; no writes | Detailed file-by-file preview after `fleet-status` flagged something |
| `just fleet-diff HOST` | `chezmoi diff` on ONE host, serial output | None | Inspecting exactly what one host would change |
| `just fleet-apply` | `chezmoi update --init` on every host (= `git pull` + re-render `chezmoi.toml` + `apply` + run_* scripts) | **Mutates remotes** | The actual deploy |
| `just fleet-apply-file PATH` | `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <PATH>` on every host (skips ansible / Brewfile) | Mutates only that one target | Vibe loop — fast feedback for one dotfile |
| `just fleet-apply-branch BRANCH` | Pin remotes to a feature branch before applying | Mutates remotes + checks out branch on remote source dir | Iterating on a topic branch across the fleet |
| `just fleet-apply-one HOST` | Apply to a single host in `--serial` mode (debug-friendly output) | Mutates that host | Targeted apply / debugging |
| `just fleet-apply-status` | **Process-liveness probe** — is a chezmoi/ansible run still going on each host? | None (read-only) | After Ctrl+C'ing controller, to see which remotes are still busy |
| `just fleet-apply-watch` | Same as `fleet-apply-status` but polls every 10s until everyone idle | None | Passive "wait for fleet to settle" cursor |
| `just fleet-apply-tail HOST` | Live-tail the latest fleet-apply log on `HOST` over a fresh SSH session | None | Re-attach to a still-running run after Ctrl+C |
| `just fleet-apply-compact` | Post-mortem summary across the fleet (final task, runtime, slow tasks, exit code) | None (reads remote logs) | After a finished run, when per-host `--tail` is too noisy |
| `just fleet-apply-kill` | `pkill -TERM` then `-KILL` chezmoi/ansible on every host | **Kills processes** | Cleanup after Ctrl+C left orphans |

> **Common naming confusion**: `fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`. The first is a pre-apply readiness probe ("would `fleet-apply` succeed right now?"), the second is a process-liveness probe ("is a `fleet-apply` still running?"). They answer different questions and are usually used in different phases of your workflow.

### Typical workflows

```bash
# Daily: push to repo, then deploy.
git push
just fleet-status              # pre-flight check — anything need attention?
just fleet-apply               # actual deploy

# Vibe loop: edit one file, push, fast-apply across fleet.
git add .config/zsh/aliases.zsh && git commit -m "..." && git push
just fleet-apply-file .config/zsh/aliases.zsh

# After Ctrl+C'ing a long fleet-apply: where am I?
just fleet-apply-status        # which hosts still running?
just fleet-apply-watch         # wait until everyone idle
just fleet-apply-tail lab-box  # re-attach to one host's log
just fleet-apply-kill          # nuke leftover orphans

# After fleet-apply finished, want a summary:
just fleet-apply-compact
```

## When to use

You edited dotfiles on the workstation, pushed to the repo's git remote, and
now want every laptop / VM / lab box to pick up the change without sshing into
each one and typing the sudo password by hand.

## When NOT to use

- This tool **does not** push the dotfiles repo itself — every remote runs
  `chezmoi update`, which does `git pull` on the remote's source dir. Your
  changes must already be reachable by the remotes (push to GitHub / your
  internal git host first).
- It does not run `just upgrade-*` on remotes. That's a separate concern; this
  tool stays scoped to chezmoi apply.
- It does not provision new hosts. Each remote must already have `chezmoi`
  installed and `chezmoi init` completed at least once.

## Readiness probe (`just fleet-status`)

`fleet-apply` defaults to `chezmoi update --init`, which is **three things in
sequence** under the hood:

1. `git -C <source> pull` — bring in new template commits
2. `chezmoi init` — re-render `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` (re-evaluates `promptBoolOnce` / `promptStringOnce` calls; **NEW prompt keys without saved answers will fail non-interactively** with `chezmoi: ... could not open a new TTY`)
3. `chezmoi apply` — render templates, write targets, run `run_*` scripts (ansible, Brewfile, etc.)

The readiness probe inspects each host once over SSH and predicts what each of
those three sub-steps would do, **without changing anything**. Cheaper than
`fleet-apply-dry-run` (which runs full `chezmoi diff`) and more actionable
than `fleet-apply-status` (which only sees live processes, not pending
drift / missing init / new prompt keys).

```bash
just fleet-status                              # all hosts, with `git fetch`
just fleet-status --hosts lab-box,vps-tokyo    # subset
just fleet-status-quick                        # skip remote `git fetch` (faster, may show stale 'behind')
just fleet-status --readiness-json | jq .      # machine-readable
```

### State matrix

The probe classifies each host into exactly one primary state and zero or
more secondary notes (e.g. a `behind` host with drift will show
`behind: 3 commits, drift: 2 files` in the notes column).

| State | Symbol | Meaning | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| `up-to-date` | ✓ green | Source dir at `origin/HEAD`, no drift, init done | Nothing to do |
| `ready-to-update` | ↻ blue | Source is behind origin → `fleet-apply` will pull + apply cleanly | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` |
| `behind` | → cyan | Same as `ready-to-update` but used when there are also other notes (drift / dirty co-existing) | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST` |
| `drift` | ⚠ yellow | Remote target was hand-edited; would trigger "could not open a new TTY" prompt without `--force`. With default `--keep-going`, applies the rest of the fleet and skips this file | `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST --force` (overwrite) OR migrate to a `*.local` override |
| `dirty` | ⚠ yellow | Remote source dir has uncommitted changes (someone hand-edited the template on the remote) | ssh in & commit/stash before applying |
| `ahead` | ? magenta | Remote source dir has local commits not on origin — `git pull` would diverge | ssh in & `git push` or reset before applying |
| `busy` | ⏳ yellow | A `chezmoi update/apply/init` or `ansible-playbook` is already running, OR the chezmoi state lock is held | Wait, then re-probe; OR `just fleet-apply-status --hosts HOST` for live state |
| `init-in-progress` | ⏳ yellow | Source dir is missing/incomplete BUT a `chezmoi update/apply/init` PID is alive — typically mid-clone, or paused at an interactive prompt in another SSH session. Distinct from `no-source` (which is permanent until human intervention) | Wait for the in-flight init to finish, OR ssh in & check the other session |
| `toml-mismatch` | ! yellow bold | The local `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` declares prompt keys (`promptBoolOnce` / `promptStringOnce` / etc.) that are missing from the remote's saved `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`. **This is the `david_ubuntu` failure mode** — `fleet-apply` will crash on this host with `chezmoi: ... could not open a new TTY` on `chezmoi init` | ssh in & re-run `chezmoi init` to answer the new prompts |
| `not-init` | ✗ red | `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` doesn't exist — host was never `chezmoi init`'d | ssh in & run `chezmoi init` interactively (one-off; needs TTY) |
| `no-source` | ✗ red | `chezmoi source-path` returns nothing or the path is not a git repo | ssh in & re-init (or fix custom `chezmoi.toml` `sourceDir =`) |
| `no-chezmoi` | ✗ red | `chezmoi` binary not found in augmented PATH | ssh in & install chezmoi (`curl https://chezmoi.io/get \| sh`) |
| `unreachable` | ✗ red | SSH connection failed (timeout, auth, host key, network) | check ssh_alias / network / sudo / 1Password agent |

### Output format

```
fleet-status — readiness probe across 6 host(s)
                                readiness probe
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ host       ┃ state                  ┃ notes                                    ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ self       │ ✓ up-to-date           │                                          │
│ hanru_mac  │ ↻ ready-to-update      │ behind: 3 commits                        │
│ ts_nas     │ ⏳ busy                │ pids=12345                               │
│ jingle207  │ ⚠ drift                │ drift: .config/mise/config.toml          │
│ david_ub   │ ! toml-mismatch        │ missing prompt keys: installTunnelTools  │
│ idc-srv    │ ✗ unreachable          │ TimeoutError: 30s                        │
└────────────┴────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘

Hints:
  ✗ unreachable (1: idc-srv)
      → check ssh_alias / network / sudo / 1Password agent
  ! toml-mismatch (1: david_ub)
      → ssh in & re-run `chezmoi init` to answer the new prompts (their default values are usually fine)
  ⏳ busy (1: ts_nas)
      → wait for the running run, OR `just fleet-apply-status --hosts HOST` for live state
  ⚠ drift (1: jingle207)
      → `just fleet-apply --hosts HOST --force` (overwrite) OR migrate to a *.local override
  ↻ ready-to-update (1: hanru_mac)
```

```text
# 96_ssh_setup.sh - Interactive SSH key setup for remote machines (shared).
# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/96_ssh_setup.zsh. Zsh-isms replaced:
#   emulate -L zsh                  → gated on $ZSH_VERSION
#   setopt localoptions pipefail    → gated on $ZSH_VERSION (bash: set -o pipefail)
#   ~/.ssh/*.pub(N)  (nullglob)     → shopt -s nullglob / setopt nullglob dispatch
#   print -u2 --                    → printf >&2
#   print "..."                     → printf
#   print -n "..."                  → printf '%s' (no newline)
#   ${key_path:t}    (basename)     → ${key_path##*/}
#   ${#existing_keys}               → ${#existing_keys[@]}
#
# Usage: ssh-setup-remote [user@]host
#
# Walks through: create key → ssh-copy-id → copy key to remote → add SSH config entries.
# See docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md for the full tutorial.

ssh-setup-remote() {
  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
    emulate -L zsh
    setopt localoptions pipefail
  else
    set -o pipefail
  fi

  local usage="Usage: ssh-setup-remote [user@]host"
  if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  local target="$1"
  local remote_user remote_host
  if [[ "$target" == *@* ]]; then
    remote_user="${target%%@*}"
    remote_host="${target#*@}"
  else
    remote_host="$target"
    remote_user=""
  fi

  # ── Step 0: Key selection ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  printf '\n%s\n' "=== SSH Key Setup for $target ==="

  local key_path=""
  local create_new=""

  printf '\nExisting keys in ~/.ssh/:\n'

  # Portable nullglob: in zsh, `*.pub(N)` made the glob expand to nothing

```text
# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
#
# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
# is just the bare hostname.
#
# Usage:
#   tv ssh-config
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
#   Enter      SSH into selected host
#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows resolved config via `ssh -G` plus a local-key existence check
# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).

[metadata]
name = "ssh-config"
description = "SSH hosts (with Include config.d/* support)"
requirements = ["ssh", "awk", "sort"]

[source]
# Emit "<source-file>\t<hostname>" so the picker shows the origin file but
# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
command = """
for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  rel=${f#$HOME/}
  awk -v src="$rel" '
    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
      }
    }' "$f"
done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2
"""
display = "{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:0})"
output = "{split:\\t:1}"

[preview]
command = """
host='{split:\\t:1}'
src='{split:\\t:0}'
echo "# defined in: $src"
echo
ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(host|hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxycommand|proxyjump|forwardagent|identityagent|localforward|remoteforward)[[:space:]]'
```
</details></tool-use>

## Exploration Summary

Based on my thorough exploration of `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi`, here are the existing helpers you'd build on for remote fleet features:

### 1. **`tsum` Helper**

**Location:**
- Shell wrapper: `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/61_tmux_summary.sh` (lines 25–142)
- Core Python script: `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py` (lines 1–953)

**What it does:**
AI-powered summary of all tmux sessions on the local machine. Queries local tmux server via `tmux list-sessions / list-windows`, constructs a structured prompt (session names, window details, optional active-pane tail), sends to a coding agent (Claude/OpenCode/Codex/Cursor), parses JSON response with closability tiers (safe/check/keep), and renders human-readable or TSV output. Caches by `sha256(prompt)[:16]` (per-host, mode-aware) with a 120s throttle window for high-churn panes.

**Output format:**
- Default (`list` mode): Rich text, one block per session with glyph (🟢/🟡/🔴), name, window count, one-liner summary, closability reason, and important windows
- `picker` mode: TSV `<session>\t<summary>` for fzf piping
- `-i/--interactive`: Picker → fzf → `tmux switch-client -t <session>` on Enter
- `--json` not supported; `--dry-run` prints the constructed prompt; `--no-cache` skips cache I/O

**Remote tmux?**
Local only. Queries `$TMUX_PANE` env var to avoid capturing its own pane output. No SSH; no multi-host support. **TSUM_TMUX_BIN** env var allows pinning a specific tmux binary (relevant when multiple versions exist and protocol-mismatch occurs).

**Related helpers:**
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary-popup.sh` — wraps tsum in a tmux popup
- `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py` — television (TV picker) integration for session browsing

### 5. **Per-Host Fan-Out Pattern (`scripts/fleet_apply.py`)**

**Parallelism implementation:**

| Aspect | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Method** | `asyncio.Semaphore(parallelism)` bounded concurrency (line 3020) |
| **Parallelism** | `--max-parallel N` flag (default auto: `min(8, len(hosts))`) OR `--serial` forces sequential |
| **Per-host execution** | `async def _bounded(st: HostStatus)` wraps `await run_one(...)` behind semaphore (lines 3029–3037) |
| **Orchestration** | `asyncio.gather(*(_bounded(st) for st in runnable))` launches all tasks at once, semaphore gates actual concurrency (line 3052) |
| **Per-host timeout** | `command_timeout` (default 1800s / 30m): wraps chezmoi remote execution in `asyncio.timeout(command_timeout)` (line 921) |
| **Connection timeout** | `connect_timeout` (default 15s): asyncssh session open wrapped in `asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout)` (line 872) |
| **SSH layer** | `asyncssh` (async, non-blocking SSH client); each host gets its own `asyncssh.connect()` coroutine |
| **Live rendering** | `Rich.live.Live` table polling every 4 FPS; parallel task updates a shared `statuses: list[HostStatus]` dict (safe because Python GIL + dict updates are atomic at the dict level) |
| **Failure handling** | Per-host rc tracked in `HostStatus.rc`; exit code = min(failed_count, 125) (line 3060) |
| **Local hosts** | Skip SSH entirely; use `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec()` for local `chezmoi` subprocess (line 679) |

**Key invariants:**
- Semaphore prevents thundering herd; soft-cap at 8 concurrent SSH connections by default
- Per-host log files written to `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log` (line 3021)
- If `--keep-going` set, one host failure doesn't kill the rest; all runnable hosts execute regardless
- Grace period logic for SIGTERM → SIGKILL (lines 732–752): 5s after proc.terminate(), force SIGKILL if still running

No `.json` or `--json` flag exists on `tsum` (summary is parsed to dict internally, only rendered to text). Fleet_apply.py uses `asyncio.Semaphore` for bounded parallelism, not simple subprocess + wait loops. The pattern is fully async/await with per-host timeouts (connect + command). # Fleet CLI Refactor & Extension Plan

## A. Architecture / File Layout

**Umbrella binary**: `bin/executable_fleet` — `uv run --script` PEP-723 header matches `bin/executable_sms:1-9`. Pinned deps:
```
asyncssh>=2.18, tyro>=0.9, rich>=13.9
```
(No new deps — every subcommand reuses what `scripts/fleet_apply.py:5-7` already pulls.)

**Shared code organization**: New package at `scripts/fleet/`:
- `scripts/fleet/__init__.py` — empty marker
- `scripts/fleet/_lib.py` — `Host` dataclass (lifted from `fleet_apply.py:62-89`), `load_hosts()` (L101-157), `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` (L95-98), `_connect_kwargs()` (L556-577), `resolve_passwords()` (L191-…), `REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH`/`REMOTE_LOG_DIR`/`LOCAL_LOG_DIR` (L243-252), the asyncssh fan-out helpers (`_bounded`, `_orchestrate` skeleton from L3019-3052), `_live_render_loop`, `_STATE_STYLE`, and a generic `run_fanout(hosts, per_host_coro, *, parallelism, serial, console)` factored out of `_run()` (L2971-3058)
- `scripts/fleet/apply.py` — current `cli()` body + all `_run_*` helpers (kill/status/tail/compact/readiness/preflight) re-exported as `main()`
- `scripts/fleet/tmux.py` — new
- `scripts/fleet/info.py` — new

**Why a package, not flat files**: shared inventory loading + asyncssh fan-out + Rich rendering belongs in one place; per-subcommand orchestration belongs in its own file. Flat `scripts/fleet_tmux.py` etc. would force each new subcommand to re-import dataclasses from `fleet_apply.py`, locking us into the legacy filename.

**bin/ binary boot**: `bin/executable_fleet` resolves the chezmoi source dir to find `scripts/fleet/`:
```python
src = subprocess.run(
    ["chezmoi", "source-path"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
).stdout.strip() or os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/chezmoi")
sys.path.insert(0, src)
from scripts.fleet import apply, tmux, info  # noqa: E402
```
Then a tiny tyro dispatch picks the subcommand. Use `tyro.extras.subcommand_cli_from_dict({"apply": apply.cli, "tmux": tmux.cli, "info": info.cli, "edit": _edit_inventory, "status": apply.status_cli, ...})` so `--help` for each sub flows naturally from the existing tyro-annotated signatures.

**Fate of `scripts/fleet_apply.py`**: becomes a 10-line shim:
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# PEP-723 header (same as today)
from scripts.fleet.apply import main
import sys
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
This keeps every `just fleet-*` recipe (which invokes `./scripts/fleet_apply.py`) working unmodified during the transition. The `from scripts.fleet.apply import main` only works because the shim is invoked via path inside the chezmoi source dir, where `scripts/` is importable relative to cwd. (For the binary path we use the sys.path.insert trick.)

## B. Subcommand Mapping

| `fleet <sub>` | Replaces / wraps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fleet apply [--hosts X] [--dry-run] [--force] ...` | `just fleet-apply`, `just fleet-apply-dry-run`, `just fleet-apply-one`, `just fleet-diff`, `just fleet-apply-file`, `just fleet-apply-branch[-force]` | One umbrella; existing flags pass through verbatim |
| `fleet status` | `just fleet-status` (readiness) | Alias for `apply --readiness` |
| `fleet status --quick` | `just fleet-status-quick` | Adds `--readiness-no-fetch` |
| `fleet status --live` | `just fleet-apply-status` | Process-liveness (existing `--status`) — disambiguate via `--live` flag since readiness vs apply-status are two different things |
| `fleet status --live --watch 10` | `just fleet-apply-watch` | |
| `fleet tail HOST[:RUN_ID]` | `just fleet-apply-tail HOST` | Positional arg |
| `fleet kill` | `just fleet-apply-kill` | Alias for `apply --kill-orphans` |
| `fleet compact [--run-id RUN_ID]` | `just fleet-apply-compact` | |
| `fleet edit` | `just fleet-edit` | Seeds template + `$EDITOR` (port the seed text from `justfile:472-476`) |
| `fleet tmux ...` | NEW | Section C |
| `fleet info ...` | NEW | Section D |

**Just recipes**: rewrite each as `fleet <sub>` wrapper — but only after `bin/fleet` exists and survives smoke. Until then `just fleet-apply` keeps calling `./scripts/fleet_apply.py` (the shim).

**No breaking changes** in flag shape — only the `fleet status` overload (readiness default, `--live` for process probe) needs a doc-call. The justfile preserves both names so muscle memory is intact.

## C. `fleet tmux` Design

**CLI shape**:
```
fleet tmux [--hosts X,Y] [--exclude Z] [--with-summary] [--json]
          [--deep] [--no-cache] [--connect-timeout N] [--serial] [--max-parallel N]
```

**Required upstream change in `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`**:
- Add `--json` + `--no-ai` flags (`--no-ai` already implied by `--json` for simplicity — pick one; recommend `--json` short-circuits before LLM)
- New short-circuit point: after `sessions = collect_sessions(deep=args.deep)` (L829), before `build_prompt` (L851):
  ```python
  if args.json:
      print(json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(s) for s in sessions], indent=2))
      return 0
  ```
- Schema is direct serialization of `Session{name, created, attached, last_attached, windows[], active_pane_tail, active_pane_skipped}` and `Window{index, name, active, cwd, cmd, panes}` — both already `@dataclass` (L208-227).
- `--no-cache` interacts naturally: `--json` skips the cache and LLM entirely, so `--no-cache` is redundant on the JSON path (still accepted for orthogonality).

**Remote dispatcher** (in `scripts/fleet/tmux.py`):
1. Try preferred path:
   ```
   if [ -x ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py ]; then
     ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py --json --deep && exit 0 || true
   fi
   ```
   (`--deep` controlled by `--deep` flag on `fleet tmux`)
2. Fallback raw capture (single bash blob over SSH):
   ```bash
   tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}\t#{session_created}\t#{session_attached}\t#{session_last_attached}' 2>/dev/null;
   echo '---';
   tmux list-windows -a -F '#{session_name}\t#{window_index}\t#{window_name}\t#{window_active}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{pane_current_command}\t#{window_panes}' 2>/dev/null
   ```
   then Python-side parser reconstructs the same JSON schema (so downstream rendering doesn't care which path was taken).
3. `rc != 0` AND empty stdout → row renders `N/A` (no tmux server, or tmux missing).

**Decision regex**: try preferred first, capture `rc + stdout`; if `rc != 0` OR `stdout.strip() == ""` OR `json.loads()` raises → fallback. Don't probe with `test -x` — combine probe and run in one ssh call.

**Aggregator output**: Rich table columns:
```
HOST | SESSIONS | WINDOWS | ATTACHED | LAST ATTACHED | TOP SESSION
```
- `SESSIONS`/`WINDOWS`: integer counts
- `ATTACHED`: count of `session.attached == True`
- `LAST ATTACHED`: max `last_attached` across sessions, rendered with `humanize` (or just `time.strftime` against `datetime.fromtimestamp`)
- `TOP SESSION`: name of session with most windows; tie → most recent `last_attached`

`--json` → emit `{"host": ..., "sessions": [...], "source": "py"|"raw"|"none", "error": "..."}` per host to stdout.

**`--with-summary`**: collect all hosts first, then ONE LLM call invoked via `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py` reading concatenated JSON from stdin (would need a new `--from-json` mode added to the summary script — note as deferred; for this round, keep `--with-summary` documented but not implemented, OR implement by calling the agent the same way the summary script does at L882-883). Recommended: implement only the JSON path now; ship `--with-summary` as a stub that errors with "not yet implemented".

## D. `fleet info` Design

**CLI shape**:
```
fleet info [--hosts X] [--exclude Y] [--ff] [--full] [--modules cpu,mem,disk,...]
          [--json] [--verbose] [--connect-timeout N] [--serial] [--max-parallel N]
```

**Module catalog** (cross-platform; each module is a small dispatch that picks linux/darwin command at runtime via `uname -s`):

| Module | Linux command | Darwin command |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `lscpu \| awk -F: '/Model name/{print $2}'` + `nproc` | `sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string` + `sysctl -n hw.ncpu` |
| `mem` | `awk '/MemTotal/{t=$2}/MemAvailable/{a=$2}END{printf "%d %d", t-a, t}' /proc/meminfo` (KB) | `sysctl -n hw.memsize` + `vm_stat \| awk '...'` for used |
| `disk` | `df -PB1 / \| awk 'NR==2{print $3,$2}'` | `df -PB1 / \| awk 'NR==2{print $3,$2}'` (same — POSIX `df`) |
| `uptime` | `awk '{print int($1)}' /proc/uptime` | `sysctl -n kern.boottime \| sed ...` |
| `load` | `awk '{print $1,$2,$3}' /proc/loadavg` | `sysctl -n vm.loadavg \| tr -d '{}'` |
| `docker` | `docker ps -q \| wc -l` + `docker ps -aq \| wc -l` (skip if `command -v docker` fails) | same |
| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi --no-pager status \| wc -l` + `git -C $(chezmoi source-path) rev-list --count HEAD..@{u}` | same |
| `gpu` | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv,noheader,nounits` (skip if absent) | `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json \| jq '...'` |
| `network` | `hostname -f` + `hostname -I \| awk '{print $1}'` | `hostname` + `ipconfig getifaddr en0` |
| `os` | `lsb_release -ds 2>/dev/null \|\| cat /etc/os-release \| awk -F= '/^PRETTY_NAME/{...}'` | `sw_vers -productName` + `sw_vers -productVersion` |

Default curated quick view: `cpu, mem, disk, load, uptime, docker, chezmoi, os` (8 modules, render in <2s/host).

**`--ff` (fastfetch)**: invoke `fastfetch --format json` over SSH; if `command -v fastfetch` fails → `"—"`. Parse and render as flat key-value table. (`fastfetch` is installed by `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:3946-…` so most hosts have it.)

**`--full`**: enumerate every module from the catalog.

**`--modules a,b,c`**: comma-split, intersect with catalog (warn on unknown).

**Wire format**: build ONE bash blob per host with `set +e` so per-module failure doesn't abort the rest. Each module emits one line of `KEY\tVALUE` (or `KEY\tERR\t<msg>`). Python-side parses; missing/err → table cell `"—"` with `--verbose` printing the error to stderr.

**Output**: Rich table with rows = hosts, columns = modules. `--json` → `{"host": ..., "modules": {"cpu": {"model": ..., "cores": ...}, ...}}` per host.

**Fallback strategy**: each per-host orchestration runs inside `try/except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)`; the row renders `host: <name>, status: N/A, error: <type>` and the run continues. Mirrors the existing per-host failure pattern in `_run_kill` at L1486-1508.

## F. Verification Plan

End-to-end:
1. `fleet apply --hosts self --dry-run` — confirms shim works and local path renders.
2. `fleet apply --hosts <remote> --dry-run` — confirms asyncssh path.
3. `fleet status` (readiness) and `fleet status --live` (process probe) — separation works.
4. `fleet tmux --hosts self` — preferred `.py --json` path (local has the script).
5. `fleet tmux --hosts <minimal-remote>` (no `tmux-session-summary.py` deployed yet) — fallback raw path.
6. `fleet tmux --hosts <no-tmux-server>` — empty session list, row shows `0` not `N/A`.
7. `fleet tmux --hosts <tmux-not-installed>` — row shows `N/A` with error in `--verbose`.
8. `fleet info` (default 8 modules).
9. `fleet info --ff` (fastfetch path).
10. `fleet info --full` (all modules including `gpu` on `no-GPU` host → `N/A`).
11. `fleet info --modules cpu,mem` (filter).
12. `fleet info --hosts <unreachable>` — asyncssh `ConnectionLost`/`OSError` → row `N/A`, run continues.
13. `fleet info --hosts <no-docker>` — `docker` cell `N/A`, others populated.
14. `just fleet-apply --hosts self --dry-run` and every other existing `just fleet-*` recipe — confirms shim preserves backward compat.
15. Run `tmux-session-summary.py --json` locally — confirms JSON schema parses and matches what `fleet tmux` fallback parser expects.

**Edge cases to specifically exercise**:
- SSH timeout (asyncssh `ConnectionLost` after `connect_timeout`) → row `N/A`
- Host where `python3` is missing (BSD/older CentOS) → preferred path fails, fallback works
- Host with `tmux 3.2` apt vs `~/.local/bin/tmux` mismatch → fallback uses whatever `tmux` resolves on remote PATH (same caveat as `TSUM_TMUX_BIN` in summary script)
- Concurrent run: `fleet apply` + `fleet info` against overlapping hosts → no shared state collision (info is read-only, doesn't touch `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/`)

## G. `backlog/bin-migration.md` content (one-shot draft for the user to commit)

**Title**: Move `~/bin/` to a less-conflict-prone location

**Status**: P? / deferred — `~/bin` works today, no immediate pain point.

**Problem statement**: `~/bin` is a common collision target — third-party installers (Anaconda, asdf, mise, custom build scripts) sometimes drop binaries there or expect it as user-owned. chezmoi's ownership of `~/bin/sms`, `~/bin/mi-router`, `~/bin/x`, plus the soon-to-exist `~/bin/fleet`, makes diagnosing "where did this binary come from" harder than it needs to be.

**Three options** (pros/cons):

1. **Stay at `~/bin/`** (current): zero migration cost; collision risk persists; convention used by half the dotfiles ecosystem so users expect it. Files affected: none. **Recommended for now.**
2. **`~/.dotfiles-bin/`**: prefix telegraphs origin; isolates chezmoi-managed CLIs from anything an installer might drop. Files affected: rename `bin/` → `dot_dotfiles-bin/` (chezmoi attribute prefix), update `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:23` PATH order, update every doc reference to `~/bin/sms`/`~/bin/mi-router`/`~/bin/fleet`, update onboarding (`bootstrap.sh` if it mentions PATH).
3. **`~/.local/share/chezmoi-bin/`** (XDG-aligned): cleanest semantic — "binaries owned by chezmoi"; but breaks the convention that `~/.local/share` is for data, not executables. Files: same enumeration as option 2 plus possibly a `dot_local/share/private_chezmoi-bin/` attribute combo to suppress backup.

**Files affected by any migration** (enumeration for future implementer):
- `bin/executable_sms` → new path
- `bin/executable_mi-router` → new path
- `bin/executable_x` → new path
- `bin/executable_sesh-preview` → new path
- `bin/executable_fleet` (post this round) → new path
- `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:23` — PATH export
- `justfile` recipes (audit for `~/bin` hardcodes)
- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, any doc mentioning `~/bin/fleet`
- `pitfalls/*.md` references (none today, but audit before migrating)

**Migration ordering**: add new path to PATH alongside old → ship `chezmoi apply` that creates new symlinks → flip docs → wait one release cycle → remove old `~/bin/` entries. Don't big-bang.

**Decision**: deferred until a real collision happens or another binary lands. Re-evaluate when `bin/` exceeds 10 entries.

10	"""
11	fleet_apply.py — Run `chezmoi update --init` (or `apply` / `diff`) across a
12	fleet of remote hosts in parallel, with optional sudo password injection.
13	
14	Why this exists:
15	    Pushing dotfile changes to N machines by hand (ssh, type password, wait,
16	    grep logs) is error-prone. This wraps that flow:
17	
18	      * Host list + connection details live in ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
19	      * Connection prefers ssh_config alias (ProxyJump, IdentityAgent, etc. all
20	        kept) — falls back to explicit hostname/user/port/identity_file.
21	      * Sudo password sources: plaintext (TOML), interactive prompt (asked once
22	        at startup), Bitwarden CLI (`bw get password <item>`), or omitted.
23	      * Per-host `no_root_machine = true` skips sudo entirely (matches the
24	        chezmoi `noRoot=true` init choice on that host).
25	      * Live Rich table of progress + per-host log files under
26	        logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log
27	
28	Exit code: number of failed hosts (0 = all good, capped at 125).
29	
30	See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md for full schema, examples, troubleshooting.
31	"""
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import asyncio
35	import dataclasses
36	import getpass
37	import os
38	import re
39	import shlex
40	import subprocess
41	import sys
42	import time
43	import tomllib
44	from datetime import datetime, timezone
45	from pathlib import Path
46	from typing import Annotated, Literal

48	import asyncssh
49	import tyro
50	from rich.console import Console
51	from rich.live import Live
52	from rich.table import Table

55	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	# Data model
57	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	
59	PasswordSourceType = Literal["plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"]
60	
61	
62	@dataclasses.dataclass
63	class Host:
64	    """One remote machine. See machines.toml schema in docs."""
65	
66	    name: str
67	    ssh_alias: str | None = None
68	    hostname: str | None = None
69	    user: str | None = None
70	    port: int | None = None
71	    identity_file: str | None = None
72	    no_root_machine: bool = False
73	    chezmoi_path: str = "auto"
74	    # When True, bypass SSH entirely and run chezmoi as a local
75	    # subprocess on the orchestrator machine. Useful for including the
76	    # control box itself in a fleet apply (e.g. you keep your own
77	    # workstation in sync with the same `just fleet-apply` invocation).
78	    # Local hosts skip all SSH-specific config (ssh_alias/hostname/
79	    # user/port/identity_file are ignored) and reuse the caller's
80	    # ambient PATH so chezmoi_path = "auto" still works without the
81	    # remote-style PATH augmentation. Sudo password injection is
82	    # skipped — chezmoi inherits the caller's tty/sudoers state.
83	    local: bool = False
84	    extra_env: dict[str, str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
85	    # Resolved later (not from TOML directly)
86	    password_source_type: PasswordSourceType = "none"
87	    password_source_arg: str | None = None  # plain value, bw item id, etc.
88	    sudo_password: str | None = None  # populated by resolve_passwords()
89	
90	
91	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
92	# TOML loading
93	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
94	
95	DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = Path(
96	    os.environ.get("FLEET_CONFIG")
97	    or (Path.home() / ".config" / "fleet" / "machines.toml")
98	).expanduser()
99	
100	
101	def load_hosts(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Host], dict]:
102	    """Parse machines.toml -> ([Host, ...], defaults dict).
103	
104	    Merges [defaults] into each host (host overrides defaults). The
105	    `password_source` table is normalized into (type, arg) on Host.
106	    """
107	    if not path.exists():
108	        raise FileNotFoundError(
109	            f"Fleet config not found: {path}\n"
110	            f"Hint: chezmoi apply seeds ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — edit it "
111	            f"to list your machines, or pass --config PATH."
112	        )
113	    with path.open("rb") as f:
114	        data = tomllib.load(f)
115	
116	    defaults = data.get("defaults", {}) or {}
117	    raw_hosts = data.get("hosts", []) or []
118	    if not raw_hosts:
119	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [[hosts]] entries defined.")
120	
121	    hosts: list[Host] = []
122	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
123	    for idx, raw in enumerate(raw_hosts):
124	        name = raw.get("name")
125	        if not name:
126	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: [[hosts]][{idx}] missing required `name`.")
127	        if name in seen_names:
128	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: duplicate host name {name!r}.")
129	        seen_names.add(name)
130	
131	        merged = {**defaults, **raw}
132	        ps = merged.pop("password_source", None) or {}
133	        ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
134	        if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):
135	            raise ValueError(
136	                f"{path}: host {name!r} has invalid password_source.type={ps_type!r}"
137	            )
138	        ps_arg = ps.get("value") if ps_type == "plain" else ps.get("item")
139	
140	        # Drop keys that aren't Host fields (e.g. defaults-only knobs we read elsewhere).
141	        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
142	        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
143	        host = Host(
144	            **host_kwargs,
145	            password_source_type=ps_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
146	            password_source_arg=ps_arg,
147	        )
148	
149	        # Validation: at least one of ssh_alias / hostname (skipped for local hosts).
150	        if not host.local and not host.ssh_alias and not host.hostname:
151	            raise ValueError(
152	                f"{path}: host {name!r} must define either `ssh_alias` "
153	                f"(preferred) or `hostname` (or set `local = true` to run "
154	                f"on the orchestrator machine without SSH)."
155	            )
156	        hosts.append(host)
157	    return hosts, defaults
158	
159	
160
