255	def build_remote_command(
256	    host: Host,
257	    mode: Literal["update", "apply", "diff"],
258	    init: bool,
259	    force: bool = False,
260	    keep_going: bool = False,
261	    run_id: str = "adhoc",
262	    keep_logs: int = 10,
263	    apply_path: str = "",
264	    branch: str = "",
265	    force_checkout: bool = False,
266	) -> str:
267	    """Build the single shell command sent over SSH.
268	
269	    Three concerns are baked in:
270	
271	    1. Sudo password injection (when host.sudo_password is set): write password
272	       to ~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass (0600 via umask 077), export
273	       CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE, run chezmoi, then `trap … EXIT` removes
274	       the pass file even if chezmoi crashes.
275	
276	    2. Pager neutralisation: `PAGER=cat` and chezmoi-specific overrides force
277	       non-paged output. ts_nas-style hosts where `bat` panics on a missing
278	       theme would otherwise hang forever in a pager subprocess (no TTY → bat
279	       still tries to spawn).
280	
281	    3. Process-group cleanup so a local Ctrl+C / SSH channel close kills the
282	       remote chezmoi tree, not just the wrapper shell:
283	         * `set -m` enables job control so each backgrounded child gets its
284	           own process group (= -$pid kills the whole tree).
285	         * `trap '… kill -TERM -$cz_pid …' INT TERM HUP` propagates the
286	           controller's signal — asyncssh sends SIGHUP when the channel
287	           closes (request_pty=True ensures the remote side delivers it).
288	         * `wait $cz_pid` then proxies chezmoi's real exit status back.
289	       Without this, an interrupted run leaves an orphan `chezmoi update`
290	       on the remote that holds the git source dir lock and burns CPU until
291	       it self-terminates.
292	    """
293	    # `--no-pager` is a chezmoi global flag — it tells chezmoi to write
294	    # paged subcommand output (diff, status) straight to stdout instead of
295	    # spawning the configured pager. Critical for non-TTY runs because
296	    # chezmoi's default pager is whatever the user configured (often bat /
297	    # less), which can panic or block forever when its own stdin/stdout
298	    # aren't a terminal. Setting `PAGER=cat` is NOT enough — chezmoi reads
299	    # its own `pager` config key and ignores PAGER.
300	    #
301	    # `chezmoi_path == "auto"` (the default) defers binary lookup to the
302	    # remote: PATH is augmented with every plausible install location
303	    # (Linuxbrew, Homebrew x86/arm64, snap, ~/.local/bin, ~/bin) so a
304	    # non-interactive shell — which doesn't source ~/.zshrc and therefore
305	    # often lacks ~/.local/bin — still finds chezmoi. To pin a specific
306	    # binary, set `chezmoi_path = "/abs/path/to/chezmoi"` per-host.
307	    # Bare "chezmoi" (no slash, no path) is treated the same as "auto" —
308	    # users who hand-wrote that value still benefit from PATH augmentation,
309	    # because rc=127 "command not found" is the most common first-run
310	    # failure on hosts where ~/.local/bin isn't in non-interactive PATH.
311	    chezmoi_path = host.chezmoi_path or "auto"
312	    if chezmoi_path == "auto" or "/" not in chezmoi_path:
313	        cz = shlex.quote(chezmoi_path if chezmoi_path != "auto" else "chezmoi")
314	        path_prefix = (
315	            'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:'
316	            '/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:'
317	            '/usr/local/bin:/snap/bin:$PATH"; '
318	        )
319	    else:
320	        cz = shlex.quote(chezmoi_path)
321	        path_prefix = ""
322	    cz_global = f"{cz} --no-pager"
323	    # `--force` makes chezmoi auto-overwrite local drift on the remote
324	    # (the "X has changed since chezmoi last wrote it" prompt) instead of
325	    # opening /dev/tty for input — we run without a PTY, so the prompt
326	    # would die with "could not open a new TTY". `--keep-going` continues
327	    # past per-file errors so one bad template doesn't abort the whole
328	    # apply. Both are off by default; opt in via CLI.
329	    #
330	    # `--force` is destructive: any hand-edits made on the remote box are
331	    # silently replaced with the canonical template render. Acceptable
332	    # for a "push the dotfiles repo to my fleet" workflow because managed
333	    # files shouldn't be edited in place.
334	    sub_flags = ""
335	    if force:
336	        sub_flags += " --force"
337	    if keep_going:
338	        sub_flags += " --keep-going"
339	    if mode == "update":
340	        sub = f"{cz_global} update{sub_flags}"
341	        if init:
342	            sub += " --init"
343	    elif mode == "apply":
344	        sub = f"{cz_global} apply{sub_flags}"
345	        # apply_path mode: scope to one target + skip run_* scripts so an
346	        # ansible / Brewfile change doesn't trigger the slow re-run when
347	        # all you wanted was to push a dotfile edit. `--exclude=scripts`
348	        # is the chezmoi knob; the path is appended last so any per-mode
349	        # flags (--force, --keep-going) come first.
350	        #
351	        # IMPORTANT: this branch deliberately bypasses `chezmoi update`,
352	        # which means the remote source dir is NOT auto-pulled. Prepend an
353	        # explicit `git pull` of the source-path so the remote checkout
354	        # has the latest commit before we re-render the target. We use
355	        # `chezmoi source-path` (no args) to discover the source dir on
356	        # the remote — works regardless of where the user installed it.
357	        # NB: when --branch is set the git prelude below replaces this
358	        # plain pull with a checkout-of-branch sequence, so we skip it
359	        # to avoid double-pulling.
360	        if apply_path and not branch:
361	            sub = (
362	                f'_src=$({cz_global} source-path) && '
363	                f'git -C "$_src" pull --ff-only --quiet && '
364	                f"{sub} --exclude=scripts {shlex.quote(apply_path)}"
365	            )
366	        elif apply_path:
367	            sub = f"{sub} --exclude=scripts {shlex.quote(apply_path)}"
368	    else:  # diff
369	        # `chezmoi diff` doesn't take --force / --keep-going — it's
370	        # read-only and never prompts.
371	        sub = f"{cz_global} diff"
372	        if apply_path:
373	            sub += f" {shlex.quote(apply_path)}"

375	    # --branch BRANCH: pin the remote source dir to a feature branch
376	    # before the chezmoi invocation, so you can iterate on a topic branch
377	    # without polluting main. Default merge strategy is --ff-only (fail
378	    # loud on divergence so you notice). --force-checkout swaps in
379	    # `reset --hard origin/BRANCH` to nuke any local divergence — useful
380	    # when you're rebasing the topic branch and want hosts to follow.
381	    #

387	        br = shlex.quote(branch)

390	        else:
391	            sync = f'git -C "$_src" merge --ff-only origin/{branch} --quiet'
392	        prelude = (
393	            f'_src=$({cz_global} source-path) && '
394	            f'git -C "$_src" fetch origin {br} --quiet && '
395	            f'git -C "$_src" checkout -B {br} origin/{branch} --quiet && '
396	            f"{sync}"

398	        # If sub already starts with a `_src=…` prefix (apply_path branch
399	        # above), strip it — the prelude defines _src already.
400	        if sub.startswith("_src="):
401	            # Find the first ' && ' after _src=... and take everything after

403	            # The apply_path branch sets sub to "_src=… && git pull && CHEZMOI…"
404	            # — we want only the CHEZMOI part. Split on ' && ' and keep the
405	            # last segment(s).
406	            parts = sub.split(" && ", 2)
407	            sub = parts[-1] if len(parts) >= 3 else sub
408	        sub = f"{prelude} && {sub}"

410	    # Belt-and-braces: if any sub-tool chezmoi invokes (git, ansible) honours
411	    # PAGER / GIT_PAGER, force them non-paged too. NB: chezmoi itself does

436	    # `wait $_cz_pid` proxies chezmoi's real exit status back to the SSH client.

455	    # sentinels) in REMOTE_LOG_DIR. Runs AFTER chezmoi finishes, BEFORE

461	            f"_keep={keep_logs}; "
462	            f"ls -1t \"$_d\"/*.log 2>/dev/null | tail -n +$((_keep+1)) | "
463	            f"  while read -r _f; do "
464	            f"    rm -f \"$_f\" \"${{_f%.log}}.exit\"; "
465	            f"  done; "

556	def _connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict:
557	    """Translate Host -> asyncssh.connect kwargs.
558	
559	    asyncssh reads ~/.ssh/config by default for the `host` arg. When ssh_alias
560	    is set we pass it as `host` and let asyncssh resolve hostname/user/port/
561	    IdentityFile/ProxyJump from ssh_config. Explicit fields override.
562	    """
563	    target = host.ssh_alias or host.hostname
564	    assert target is not None  # validated in load_hosts
565	    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
566	    # known_hosts=None tells asyncssh to skip its own check; we still rely on
567	    # the user having ssh'd manually first (StrictHostKeyChecking is enforced
568	    # implicitly by them adding it to ~/.ssh/known_hosts ahead of time).
569	    # Switching to known_hosts=() would force strict but reject every new host.
570	    if host.user:
571	        kwargs["username"] = host.user
572	    if host.port:
573	        kwargs["port"] = host.port
574	    if host.identity_file:
575	        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
576	    return kwargs

579	def _gc_local_logs(keep: int) -> None:
580	    """Trim LOCAL_LOG_DIR to the `keep` most recent .log files (+ .exit).
581	
582	    Mirrors the remote GC done by build_remote_command. keep<=0 disables.
583	    Silent on errors (best-effort cleanup).
584	    """
585	    if keep <= 0:
586	        return
587	    try:
588	        logs = sorted(
589	            LOCAL_LOG_DIR.glob("*.log"),
590	            key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
591	            reverse=True,
592	        )
593	    except OSError:
594	        return
595	    for stale in logs[keep:]:
596	        for ext in (".log", ".exit"):
597	            try:
598	                (LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{stale.stem}{ext}").unlink(missing_ok=True)
599	            except OSError:
600	                pass

619	    and `~/.local/share/chezmoi` source. Output is streamed to the same
620	    per-host log file used by SSH hosts so the rich live table is

630	    chezmoi_bin = host.chezmoi_path if (host.chezmoi_path and host.chezmoi_path != "auto") else "chezmoi"

636	    elif mode == "apply":

639	        argv.append("diff")

641	        if force:
642	            argv.append("--force")
643	        if keep_going:

646	    # Mirrors build_remote_command's apply_path branch above.

659	            f"(local source is your editor's working tree; switch branches "

661	        )
662	    log_fp.write(f"# argv: {argv}\n\n")

665	    # so `just fleet-apply-status` / `--tail self` (= local) can find this run
666	    # using the same code path as SSH hosts. Also drop a .exit sentinel when
667	    # done. log_dir.name is the timestamp like "20260422T140446Z".
668	    LOCAL_LOG_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
669	    cache_log = LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{log_dir.name}.log"
670	    cache_exit = LOCAL_LOG_DIR / f"{log_dir.name}.exit"
671	    cache_exit.unlink(missing_ok=True)
672	    cache_fp = cache_log.open("w", buffering=1)

675	    proc = None

677	    try:
678	        status.state = "running"
679	        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
680	            *argv,
681	            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
682	            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
683	            env=env,
684	        )
685	
686	        async def _drain(stream: asyncio.StreamReader, prefix: str) -> None:
687	            while True:
688	                line = await stream.readline()
689	                if not line:
690	                    return
691	                text = line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").rstrip("\n")
692	                log_fp.write(f"[{prefix}] {text}\n")
693	                cache_fp.write(f"{text}\n")  # plain combined for tail -F
694	                status.last_line = text
695	                if prefix == "err":
696	                    stderr_lines.append(text)
697	
698	        async with asyncio.timeout(command_timeout):
699	            # Spawn the three coroutines but key the wait on a kill -0 poll —
700	            # NOT on proc.wait() OR an asyncio.gather of all three. Reason:
701	            # chezmoi's run_onchange_* scripts (ansible, brew bundle, mas,
702	            # etc.) routinely leave background children that inherit our
703	            # stdout/stderr fds and outlive their parent script.
704	            #
705	            # Two layers of asyncio quirk make this tricky:
706	            #   1. asyncio.gather(_drain, _drain, proc.wait) blocks because
707	            #      _drain waits on stream EOF, which only fires when ALL fd
708	            #      holders close — orphan grandchildren never close ours.
709	            #   2. proc.wait() ALONE also blocks: asyncio's
710	            #      BaseSubprocessTransport._try_finish only fires
711	            #      _process_exited when proc.returncode is set AND all
712	            #      stdin/stdout/stderr pipes are closed. So even
713	            #      `await proc.wait()` waits for the orphans.
714	            #
715	            # Workaround: poll `os.kill(pid, 0)` (signal 0 = existence check,
716	            # doesn't actually signal) at 100ms intervals. When that throws
717	            # ProcessLookupError, chezmoi itself is gone — the orphans are
718	            # someone else's problem. We don't waitpid() directly because
719	            # asyncio's child watcher owns the zombie reap.
720	            #
721	            # See pitfalls/fleet-apply-self-stuck-running.md for the full
722	            # debugging story including the failed first-fix attempt.
723	            stdout_task = asyncio.create_task(_drain(proc.stdout, "out"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
724	            stderr_task = asyncio.create_task(_drain(proc.stderr, "err"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
725	
726	            async def _wait_for_chezmoi_exit() -> None:
727	                while True:
728	                    try:
729	                        os.kill(proc.pid, 0)
730	                        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
731	                    except ProcessLookupError:
732	                        # chezmoi is gone. Give asyncio's watcher up to 5s to
733	                        # set returncode (it'll do so once the SIGCHLD fires
734	                        # and the child watcher reaps).
735	                        for _ in range(50):
736	                            if proc.returncode is not None:
737	                                return
738	                            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
739	                        return

1459	def _run_kill(
1460	    console: Console, selected: list[Host], connect_timeout: int
1461	) -> int:
1462	    """Connect to each host and SIGTERM stray chezmoi/ansible-playbook processes.
1463	
1464	    Use case: a previous fleet-apply was Ctrl+C'd, the local SSH client died
1465	    before the remote wrapper's trap could fire, and `chezmoi update` is now
1466	    an orphan holding the source-dir git lock. This sub-command does no
1467	    chezmoi work — it just runs `pkill -TERM` for the SSH user.
1468	
1469	    Output is direct stdout (no Live table — the operation is fast and
1470	    one-shot, table refresh would mostly show empty rows).
1471	    """
1472	    # `|| true` so pkill returning 1 (= no match) doesn't trip set -e.
1473	    # Two-pass: chezmoi first, then ansible-playbook (chezmoi spawns ansible).
1474	    kill_cmd = (
1475	        "for p in chezmoi ansible-playbook ansible; do "
1476	        "  pkill -TERM -u \"$(id -un)\" -x \"$p\" 2>/dev/null || true; "
1477	        "done; "
1478	        "sleep 1; "
1479	        "for p in chezmoi ansible-playbook ansible; do "
1480	        "  pkill -KILL -u \"$(id -un)\" -x \"$p\" 2>/dev/null || true; "
1481	        "done; "
1482	        "echo done"
1483	    )
1484	    failures = 0
1485	
1486	    async def _kill_one(h: Host) -> None:
1487	        nonlocal failures
1488	        if h.local:
1489	            # Local hosts share the orchestrator's process namespace; killing
1490	            # `chezmoi` here would kill THIS process if `just fleet-apply
1491	            # --kill-orphans` was itself launched from a chezmoi wrapper.
1492	            # Use plain `pkill` outside fleet-apply if you actually need this.
1493	            console.print(f"[yellow]·[/] {h.name} (local) — skipped")
1494	            return
1495	        target = h.ssh_alias or h.hostname
1496	        try:
1497	            async with asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout):
1498	                conn = await asyncssh.connect(**_connect_kwargs(h))
1499	            async with conn:
1500	                result = await conn.run(kill_cmd, check=False)
1501	            console.print(
1502	                f"[green]✓[/] {h.name} ({target}) "
1503	                f"rc={result.exit_status} "
1504	                f"{(result.stdout or '').strip()}"
1505	            )
1506	        except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError) as e:
1507	            failures += 1
1508	            console.print(f"[red]✗[/] {h.name} ({target}) {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
1509	
1510	    async def _orchestrate() -> None:
1511	        await asyncio.gather(*(_kill_one(h) for h in selected))
1512	
1513	    console.print(

1515	        f"(SIGTERM → 1s → SIGKILL on chezmoi/ansible-playbook/ansible)"
1516	    )
1517	    asyncio.run(_orchestrate())
1518	    return min(failures, 125)

266	    """Query the tmux server for every session + its windows.

282	            continue

326	def _capture_active_pane(session: str, wins: list[Window], my_pane: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
327	    """Visible-area capture of the session's active window's active pane.
328	
329	    Returns (text, skipped). `skipped=True` when the target pane is the one
330	    running this script — capturing it would include `tsum`'s own output
331	    (the prompt, the previous summary if any), which pollutes the LLM input
332	    and produces a recursive-looking session description.
333	
334	    Capture window is sized to the pane's actual height, clamped to
335	    [_DEEP_MIN_LINES, _DEEP_MAX_LINES]. Smaller than ~20 lines is usually
336	    useless; larger than ~100 dominates the prompt and risks leaking lots
337	    of scrollback content.
338	    """
339	    active = next((w for w in wins if w.active), wins[0] if wins else None)
340	    if active is None:
341	        return "", False
342	    target = f"{session}:{active.index}"
343	
344	    # Self-capture guard. `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}'` returns
345	    # the active pane of the target; compare against $TMUX_PANE.
346	    if my_pane:
347	        target_pane = _tmux(
348	            "display-message", "-p", "-t", target, "#{pane_id}"
349	        ).strip()
350	        if target_pane and target_pane == my_pane:
351	            return "", True
352	
353	    # Size the capture to the pane's actual visible height.
354	    height_str = _tmux(
355	        "display-message", "-p", "-t", target, "#{pane_height}"
356	    ).strip()
357	    try:
358	        height = int(height_str)
359	    except ValueError:
360	        height = 40  # reasonable fallback
361	    lines = max(_DEEP_MIN_LINES, min(height, _DEEP_MAX_LINES))
362	
363	    text = _tmux(
364	        "capture-pane", "-p", "-S", f"-{lines}", "-t", target
365	    ).rstrip()
366	    return text, False

370	# Cache (keyed by full-prompt hash)
371	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
372	def cache_path(deep: bool) -> Path:
373	    """Per-host, per-mode cache file. Splitting deep / shallow into two slots
374	    means toggling --deep / --shallow doesn't overwrite the other mode's
375	    latest cached summary — each can be served independently when its own
376	    prompt-hash hits.
377	    """
378	    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME") or os.path.expanduser("~/.cache")
379	    d = Path(base) / "tmux-session-summary"
380	    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
381	    host = socket.gethostname().split(".")[0] or "host"
382	    mode = "deep" if deep else "shallow"
383	    return d / f"{host}-{mode}.json"
384	
385	
386	# Bump when the cache schema changes. Mismatched-version files are silently
387	# ignored and overwritten on next refresh.
388	#   v2 → v3: structure signature renamed to full-prompt hash (`sig` →
389	#            `prompt_hash`); `ttl_seconds` dropped (no longer meaningful
390	#            under hash-based invalidation).
391	_CACHE_VERSION = "v3"
392	
393	
394	def lookup_cache(prompt_hash: str, deep: bool) -> tuple[list[dict] | None, str]:
395	    """Return (summaries, reason) where reason ∈ {"hit", "throttled", "miss"}.
396	
397	    - "hit":       cached prompt_hash matches → identical LLM input,
398	                   identical answer, reuse regardless of age.
399	    - "throttled": prompt_hash differs but the cache is younger than
400	                   TSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL → reuse stale summary to
401	                   absorb high-frequency churn (htop/watch/progress bars).
402	    - "miss":      stale and out-of-throttle, or no cache at all → caller
403	                   should hit the LLM.
404	    """
405	    p = cache_path(deep)
406	    if not p.is_file():
407	        return None, "miss"
408	    try:
409	        data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
410	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
411	        return None, "miss"
412	    if data.get("version") != _CACHE_VERSION:
413	        return None, "miss"
414	    summaries = data.get("sessions")
415	    if not isinstance(summaries, list):
416	        return None, "miss"
417	
418	    if data.get("prompt_hash") == prompt_hash:
419	        return summaries, "hit"

```text
7:## Cross-file maintenance rules
19:| `scripts/fleet_apply.py` / `justfile` `fleet-*` recipes / `dot_config/fleet/` / sudo helper consumption | [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md) | — |
149:**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `fleet_apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
151:### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
153:Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
156:- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
158:- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
161:- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
162:  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
163:  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
165:  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
```
</details></tool-use>

# Fleet CLI Refactor & Extension Plan

## A. Architecture / File Layout

**Umbrella binary**: `bin/executable_fleet` — `uv run --script` PEP-723 header matches `bin/executable_sms:1-9`. Pinned deps:
```
asyncssh>=2.18, tyro>=0.9, rich>=13.9
```
(No new deps — every subcommand reuses what `scripts/fleet_apply.py:5-7` already pulls.)

**Shared code organization**: New package at `scripts/fleet/`:
- `scripts/fleet/__init__.py` — empty marker
- `scripts/fleet/_lib.py` — `Host` dataclass (lifted from `fleet_apply.py:62-89`), `load_hosts()` (L101-157), `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` (L95-98), `_connect_kwargs()` (L556-577), `resolve_passwords()` (L191-…), `REMOTE_SUDO_PASS_PATH`/`REMOTE_LOG_DIR`/`LOCAL_LOG_DIR` (L243-252), the asyncssh fan-out helpers (`_bounded`, `_orchestrate` skeleton from L3019-3052), `_live_render_loop`, `_STATE_STYLE`, and a generic `run_fanout(hosts, per_host_coro, *, parallelism, serial, console)` factored out of `_run()` (L2971-3058)
- `scripts/fleet/apply.py` — current `cli()` body + all `_run_*` helpers (kill/status/tail/compact/readiness/preflight) re-exported as `main()`
- `scripts/fleet/tmux.py` — new
- `scripts/fleet/info.py` — new

**Why a package, not flat files**: shared inventory loading + asyncssh fan-out + Rich rendering belongs in one place; per-subcommand orchestration belongs in its own file. Flat `scripts/fleet_tmux.py` etc. would force each new subcommand to re-import dataclasses from `fleet_apply.py`, locking us into the legacy filename.

**bin/ binary boot**: `bin/executable_fleet` resolves the chezmoi source dir to find `scripts/fleet/`:
```python
src = subprocess.run(
    ["chezmoi", "source-path"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
).stdout.strip() or os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/chezmoi")
sys.path.insert(0, src)
from scripts.fleet import apply, tmux, info  # noqa: E402
```
Then a tiny tyro dispatch picks the subcommand. Use `tyro.extras.subcommand_cli_from_dict({"apply": apply.cli, "tmux": tmux.cli, "info": info.cli, "edit": _edit_inventory, "status": apply.status_cli, ...})` so `--help` for each sub flows naturally from the existing tyro-annotated signatures.

**Fate of `scripts/fleet_apply.py`**: becomes a 10-line shim:
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# PEP-723 header (same as today)
from scripts.fleet.apply import main
import sys
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
This keeps every `just fleet-*` recipe (which invokes `./scripts/fleet_apply.py`) working unmodified during the transition. The `from scripts.fleet.apply import main` only works because the shim is invoked via path inside the chezmoi source dir, where `scripts/` is importable relative to cwd. (For the binary path we use the sys.path.insert trick.)

## B. Subcommand Mapping

| `fleet <sub>` | Replaces / wraps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fleet apply [--hosts X] [--dry-run] [--force] ...` | `just fleet-apply`, `just fleet-apply-dry-run`, `just fleet-apply-one`, `just fleet-diff`, `just fleet-apply-file`, `just fleet-apply-branch[-force]` | One umbrella; existing flags pass through verbatim |
| `fleet status` | `just fleet-status` (readiness) | Alias for `apply --readiness` |
| `fleet status --quick` | `just fleet-status-quick` | Adds `--readiness-no-fetch` |
| `fleet status --live` | `just fleet-apply-status` | Process-liveness (existing `--status`) — disambiguate via `--live` flag since readiness vs apply-status are two different things |
| `fleet status --live --watch 10` | `just fleet-apply-watch` | |
| `fleet tail HOST[:RUN_ID]` | `just fleet-apply-tail HOST` | Positional arg |
| `fleet kill` | `just fleet-apply-kill` | Alias for `apply --kill-orphans` |
| `fleet compact [--run-id RUN_ID]` | `just fleet-apply-compact` | |
| `fleet edit` | `just fleet-edit` | Seeds template + `$EDITOR` (port the seed text from `justfile:472-476`) |
| `fleet tmux ...` | NEW | Section C |
| `fleet info ...` | NEW | Section D |

**Just recipes**: rewrite each as `fleet <sub>` wrapper — but only after `bin/fleet` exists and survives smoke. Until then `just fleet-apply` keeps calling `./scripts/fleet_apply.py` (the shim).

**No breaking changes** in flag shape — only the `fleet status` overload (readiness default, `--live` for process probe) needs a doc-call. The justfile preserves both names so muscle memory is intact.

## C. `fleet tmux` Design

**CLI shape**:
```
fleet tmux [--hosts X,Y] [--exclude Z] [--with-summary] [--json]
          [--deep] [--no-cache] [--connect-timeout N] [--serial] [--max-parallel N]
```

**Required upstream change in `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`**:
- Add `--json` + `--no-ai` flags (`--no-ai` already implied by `--json` for simplicity — pick one; recommend `--json` short-circuits before LLM)
- New short-circuit point: after `sessions = collect_sessions(deep=args.deep)` (L829), before `build_prompt` (L851):
  ```python
  if args.json:
      print(json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(s) for s in sessions], indent=2))
      return 0
  ```
- Schema is direct serialization of `Session{name, created, attached, last_attached, windows[], active_pane_tail, active_pane_skipped}` and `Window{index, name, active, cwd, cmd, panes}` — both already `@dataclass` (L208-227).
- `--no-cache` interacts naturally: `--json` skips the cache and LLM entirely, so `--no-cache` is redundant on the JSON path (still accepted for orthogonality).

**Remote dispatcher** (in `scripts/fleet/tmux.py`):
1. Try preferred path:
   ```
   if [ -x ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py ]; then
     ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py --json --deep && exit 0 || true
   fi
   ```
   (`--deep` controlled by `--deep` flag on `fleet tmux`)
2. Fallback raw capture (single bash blob over SSH):
   ```bash
   tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}\t#{session_created}\t#{session_attached}\t#{session_last_attached}' 2>/dev/null;
   echo '---';
   tmux list-windows -a -F '#{session_name}\t#{window_index}\t#{window_name}\t#{window_active}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{pane_current_command}\t#{window_panes}' 2>/dev/null
   ```
   then Python-side parser reconstructs the same JSON schema (so downstream rendering doesn't care which path was taken).
3. `rc != 0` AND empty stdout → row renders `N/A` (no tmux server, or tmux missing).

**Decision regex**: try preferred first, capture `rc + stdout`; if `rc != 0` OR `stdout.strip() == ""` OR `json.loads()` raises → fallback. Don't probe with `test -x` — combine probe and run in one ssh call.

**Aggregator output**: Rich table columns:
```
HOST | SESSIONS | WINDOWS | ATTACHED | LAST ATTACHED | TOP SESSION
```
- `SESSIONS`/`WINDOWS`: integer counts
- `ATTACHED`: count of `session.attached == True`
- `LAST ATTACHED`: max `last_attached` across sessions, rendered with `humanize` (or just `time.strftime` against `datetime.fromtimestamp`)
- `TOP SESSION`: name of session with most windows; tie → most recent `last_attached`

`--json` → emit `{"host": ..., "sessions": [...], "source": "py"|"raw"|"none", "error": "..."}` per host to stdout.

**`--with-summary`**: collect all hosts first, then ONE LLM call invoked via `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py` reading concatenated JSON from stdin (would need a new `--from-json` mode added to the summary script — note as deferred; for this round, keep `--with-summary` documented but not implemented, OR implement by calling the agent the same way the summary script does at L882-883). Recommended: implement only the JSON path now; ship `--with-summary` as a stub that errors with "not yet implemented".

## D. `fleet info` Design

**CLI shape**:
```
fleet info [--hosts X] [--exclude Y] [--ff] [--full] [--modules cpu,mem,disk,...]
          [--json] [--verbose] [--connect-timeout N] [--serial] [--max-parallel N]
```

**Module catalog** (cross-platform; each module is a small dispatch that picks linux/darwin command at runtime via `uname -s`):

| Module | Linux command | Darwin command |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `lscpu \| awk -F: '/Model name/{print $2}'` + `nproc` | `sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string` + `sysctl -n hw.ncpu` |
| `mem` | `awk '/MemTotal/{t=$2}/MemAvailable/{a=$2}END{printf "%d %d", t-a, t}' /proc/meminfo` (KB) | `sysctl -n hw.memsize` + `vm_stat \| awk '...'` for used |
| `disk` | `df -PB1 / \| awk 'NR==2{print $3,$2}'` | `df -PB1 / \| awk 'NR==2{print $3,$2}'` (same — POSIX `df`) |
| `uptime` | `awk '{print int($1)}' /proc/uptime` | `sysctl -n kern.boottime \| sed ...` |
| `load` | `awk '{print $1,$2,$3}' /proc/loadavg` | `sysctl -n vm.loadavg \| tr -d '{}'` |
| `docker` | `docker ps -q \| wc -l` + `docker ps -aq \| wc -l` (skip if `command -v docker` fails) | same |
| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi --no-pager status \| wc -l` + `git -C $(chezmoi source-path) rev-list --count HEAD..@{u}` | same |
| `gpu` | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv,noheader,nounits` (skip if absent) | `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json \| jq '...'` |
| `network` | `hostname -f` + `hostname -I \| awk '{print $1}'` | `hostname` + `ipconfig getifaddr en0` |
| `os` | `lsb_release -ds 2>/dev/null \|\| cat /etc/os-release \| awk -F= '/^PRETTY_NAME/{...}'` | `sw_vers -productName` + `sw_vers -productVersion` |

Default curated quick view: `cpu, mem, disk, load, uptime, docker, chezmoi, os` (8 modules, render in <2s/host).

**`--ff` (fastfetch)**: invoke `fastfetch --format json` over SSH; if `command -v fastfetch` fails → `"—"`. Parse and render as flat key-value table. (`fastfetch` is installed by `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:3946-…` so most hosts have it.)

**`--full`**: enumerate every module from the catalog.

**`--modules a,b,c`**: comma-split, intersect with catalog (warn on unknown).

**Wire format**: build ONE bash blob per host with `set +e` so per-module failure doesn't abort the rest. Each module emits one line of `KEY\tVALUE` (or `KEY\tERR\t<msg>`). Python-side parses; missing/err → table cell `"—"` with `--verbose` printing the error to stderr.

**Output**: Rich table with rows = hosts, columns = modules. `--json` → `{"host": ..., "modules": {"cpu": {"model": ..., "cores": ...}, ...}}` per host.

**Fallback strategy**: each per-host orchestration runs inside `try/except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)`; the row renders `host: <name>, status: N/A, error: <type>` and the run continues. Mirrors the existing per-host failure pattern in `_run_kill` at L1486-1508.

## F. Verification Plan

End-to-end:
1. `fleet apply --hosts self --dry-run` — confirms shim works and local path renders.
2. `fleet apply --hosts <remote> --dry-run` — confirms asyncssh path.
3. `fleet status` (readiness) and `fleet status --live` (process probe) — separation works.
4. `fleet tmux --hosts self` — preferred `.py --json` path (local has the script).
5. `fleet tmux --hosts <minimal-remote>` (no `tmux-session-summary.py` deployed yet) — fallback raw path.
6. `fleet tmux --hosts <no-tmux-server>` — empty session list, row shows `0` not `N/A`.
7. `fleet tmux --hosts <tmux-not-installed>` — row shows `N/A` with error in `--verbose`.
8. `fleet info` (default 8 modules).
9. `fleet info --ff` (fastfetch path).
10. `fleet info --full` (all modules including `gpu` on `no-GPU` host → `N/A`).
11. `fleet info --modules cpu,mem` (filter).
12. `fleet info --hosts <unreachable>` — asyncssh `ConnectionLost`/`OSError` → row `N/A`, run continues.
13. `fleet info --hosts <no-docker>` — `docker` cell `N/A`, others populated.
14. `just fleet-apply --hosts self --dry-run` and every other existing `just fleet-*` recipe — confirms shim preserves backward compat.
15. Run `tmux-session-summary.py --json` locally — confirms JSON schema parses and matches what `fleet tmux` fallback parser expects.

**Edge cases to specifically exercise**:
- SSH timeout (asyncssh `ConnectionLost` after `connect_timeout`) → row `N/A`
- Host where `python3` is missing (BSD/older CentOS) → preferred path fails, fallback works
- Host with `tmux 3.2` apt vs `~/.local/bin/tmux` mismatch → fallback uses whatever `tmux` resolves on remote PATH (same caveat as `TSUM_TMUX_BIN` in summary script)
- Concurrent run: `fleet apply` + `fleet info` against overlapping hosts → no shared state collision (info is read-only, doesn't touch `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/`)

## G. `backlog/bin-migration.md` content (one-shot draft for the user to commit)

**Title**: Move `~/bin/` to a less-conflict-prone location

**Status**: P? / deferred — `~/bin` works today, no immediate pain point.

**Problem statement**: `~/bin` is a common collision target — third-party installers (Anaconda, asdf, mise, custom build scripts) sometimes drop binaries there or expect it as user-owned. chezmoi's ownership of `~/bin/sms`, `~/bin/mi-router`, `~/bin/x`, plus the soon-to-exist `~/bin/fleet`, makes diagnosing "where did this binary come from" harder than it needs to be.

**Three options** (pros/cons):

1. **Stay at `~/bin/`** (current): zero migration cost; collision risk persists; convention used by half the dotfiles ecosystem so users expect it. Files affected: none. **Recommended for now.**
2. **`~/.dotfiles-bin/`**: prefix telegraphs origin; isolates chezmoi-managed CLIs from anything an installer might drop. Files affected: rename `bin/` → `dot_dotfiles-bin/` (chezmoi attribute prefix), update `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:23` PATH order, update every doc reference to `~/bin/sms`/`~/bin/mi-router`/`~/bin/fleet`, update onboarding (`bootstrap.sh` if it mentions PATH).
3. **`~/.local/share/chezmoi-bin/`** (XDG-aligned): cleanest semantic — "binaries owned by chezmoi"; but breaks the convention that `~/.local/share` is for data, not executables. Files: same enumeration as option 2 plus possibly a `dot_local/share/private_chezmoi-bin/` attribute combo to suppress backup.

**Files affected by any migration** (enumeration for future implementer):
- `bin/executable_sms` → new path
- `bin/executable_mi-router` → new path
- `bin/executable_x` → new path
- `bin/executable_sesh-preview` → new path
- `bin/executable_fleet` (post this round) → new path
- `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:23` — PATH export
- `justfile` recipes (audit for `~/bin` hardcodes)
- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, any doc mentioning `~/bin/fleet`
- `pitfalls/*.md` references (none today, but audit before migrating)

**Migration ordering**: add new path to PATH alongside old → ship `chezmoi apply` that creates new symlinks → flip docs → wait one release cycle → remove old `~/bin/` entries. Don't big-bang.

**Decision**: deferred until a real collision happens or another binary lands. Re-evaluate when `bin/` exceeds 10 entries.

112	        )
113	    with path.open("rb") as f:
114	        data = tomllib.load(f)
115	
116	    defaults = data.get("defaults", {}) or {}
117	    raw_hosts = data.get("hosts", []) or []
118	    if not raw_hosts:
119	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [[hosts]] entries defined.")
120	
121	    hosts: list[Host] = []
122	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
123	    for idx, raw in enumerate(raw_hosts):
124	        name = raw.get("name")
125	        if not name:
126	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: [[hosts]][{idx}] missing required `name`.")
127	        if name in seen_names:
128	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: duplicate host name {name!r}.")
129	        seen_names.add(name)
130	
131	        merged = {**defaults, **raw}
132	        ps = merged.pop("password_source", None) or {}
133	        ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
134	        if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):
135	            raise ValueError(
136	                f"{path}: host {name!r} has invalid password_source.type={ps_type!r}"
137	            )
138	        ps_arg = ps.get("value") if ps_type == "plain" else ps.get("item")
139	
140	        # Drop keys that aren't Host fields (e.g. defaults-only knobs we read elsewhere).
141	        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
142	        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
143	        host = Host(
144	            **host_kwargs,
145	            password_source_type=ps_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
146	            password_source_arg=ps_arg,
147	        )
148	
149	        # Validation: at least one of ssh_alias / hostname (skipped for local hosts).
150	        if not host.local and not host.ssh_alias and not host.hostname:
151	            raise ValueError(
152	                f"{path}: host {name!r} must define either `ssh_alias` "
153	                f"(preferred) or `hostname` (or set `local = true` to run "
154	                f"on the orchestrator machine without SSH)."
155	            )
156	        hosts.append(host)
157	    return hosts, defaults
158	
159	
160

```md
# Plan: `fleet` umbrella CLI — extend fleet system with `tmux` / `info` subcommands

## Context

The fleet system (`scripts/fleet_apply.py`) is mature for `chezmoi update --init` orchestration but exposes only `just fleet-*` recipes — which fail outside the chezmoi source dir tree. Two new ops needs:

1. **Cross-host tmux session visibility**: multiple remote machines accumulate stale tmux sessions; the local `tsum` is local-only and AI-driven. Want a quick "what's open where" summary across the fleet.
2. **Cross-host system status**: fastfetch is installed everywhere via the `devtools` ansible role but never queried in aggregate. Want CPU/RAM/disk/uptime/load/docker glance across hosts.

User-locked design choices (asked & answered before this plan):
- **`~/bin/` stays** — bin/ relocation deferred to `backlog/bin-migration.md`
- **Umbrella `fleet` binary** with subcommands (`fleet apply / status / tmux / info / edit / tail / kill / compact`), matches `git`/`gh`/`chezmoi` pattern
- **Remote tmux**: prefer deployed `~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py --json`, fallback to raw `tmux list-sessions -F …` when missing/broken
- **`fleet info`**: default curated quick view; `--ff` runs fastfetch JSON dump; `--full` runs all built-in modules; `--modules a,b,c` lets user select; per-module fallback → render `"—"` instead of failing the host

## Architecture

\```
bin/executable_fleet              ← new umbrella, uv-script
  → discovers chezmoi source-path
  → sys.path.insert + dispatches to scripts.fleet.<sub>.cli

scripts/fleet/                    ← new package
  __init__.py                     (empty marker)
  _lib.py                         (Host, load_hosts, _connect_kwargs,
                                   resolve_passwords, run_fanout,
                                   REMOTE_*/LOCAL_LOG_DIR constants)
  apply.py                        (lifted from current fleet_apply.py)
  tmux.py                         (new)
  info.py                         (new)

scripts/fleet_apply.py            ← becomes 10-line shim
                                   (preserves `./scripts/fleet_apply.py` callers)
\```

**Why this shape**: shared inventory loading + asyncssh fan-out + Rich rendering belongs in one place (`_lib.py`); each subcommand keeps its orchestration logic in its own file. Avoids re-importing dataclasses from a `fleet_apply.py` filename that no longer describes the scope.

**Why an umbrella binary (not separate `fleet-tmux`/`fleet-info`)**: tyro supports `subcommand_cli_from_dict` natively; single PATH entry; consistent `fleet --help` discoverability; bin/ stays small.

**Backward compat**: `scripts/fleet_apply.py` keeps its current shebang + PEP-723 header; body becomes `from scripts.fleet.apply import main; sys.exit(main())`. Every `just fleet-*` recipe continues to call `./scripts/fleet_apply.py …` unchanged during the transition. Justfile recipes get rewritten as `fleet <sub>` wrappers AFTER the binary is smoked.

## Files (new / modified)

| File | Change | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/executable_fleet` (NEW) | uv-script (`#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script`, PEP-723 deps: `asyncssh>=2.18, tyro>=0.9, rich>=13.9`); locates `chezmoi source-path`, dispatches to `scripts.fleet.*.cli` | Single binary, PATH-discoverable from anywhere |
| `scripts/fleet/__init__.py` (NEW) | Empty package marker | Make `scripts.fleet` importable |
| `scripts/fleet/_lib.py` (NEW) | `Host` (from `fleet_apply.py:62-89`), `load_hosts` (L101-157), `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` (L95), `_connect_kwargs` (L556-577), `resolve_passwords` (L191+), `LOCAL_LOG_DIR`/`REMOTE_*` constants (L243-252), generic `async def run_fanout(hosts, per_host_coro, *, parallelism, serial, console)` carved from `_run()` (L2971-3058) | DRY across apply/tmux/info subcommands |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` (NEW) | Current `cli()` body + all `_run_*` helpers + `build_remote_command` + `_classify_drift`; entrypoint `def main()` | Existing logic, just relocated |
| `scripts/fleet/tmux.py` (NEW) | `cli()` for `fleet tmux`, remote dispatcher (preferred `.py --json` + raw fallback), Rich table | See § fleet tmux |
| `scripts/fleet/info.py` (NEW) | `cli()` for `fleet info`, module catalog with linux/darwin dispatch, fastfetch path, per-module fallback | See § fleet info |
| `scripts/fleet_apply.py` (MODIFY) | Body → `from scripts.fleet.apply import main; sys.exit(main())`. Keep shebang + PEP-723 header. | Backward compat for `just fleet-*` recipes |
| `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py` (MODIFY) | Insert `--json` flag in `parse_args` (after L818); short-circuit at L829 after `collect_sessions(deep=args.deep)`: `if args.json: print(json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(s) for s in sessions], default=str)); return 0` | Reuse existing dataclasses, avoid LLM call when fleet just needs raw data |
| `justfile` (MODIFY) | Add `fleet *ARGS: fleet {{ARGS}}` recipe. Leave the 14 existing `fleet-*` recipes as-is for now (they still call `./scripts/fleet_apply.py` which is now a shim). Optionally add `fleet-tmux` / `fleet-info` wrappers for parity. | Muscle memory + new helpers both available |
| `CLAUDE.md` (MODIFY) | Update the cross-file maintenance row at L7-19 from `scripts/fleet_apply.py / justfile fleet-*…` to `bin/executable_fleet / scripts/fleet/ / justfile fleet-*…`. Still points at `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`. | Track new surface |
| `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` (MODIFY) | New sections: `## Umbrella binary` (path discovery, `fleet --help` overview), `## fleet tmux`, `## fleet info`. Document `fleet status` overload (readiness default vs `--live` for process probe). | Single doc anchor for the whole fleet surface |
| `backlog/bin-migration.md` (NEW) | One-shot draft (see § backlog content) | Per project-knowledge-harness convention; captures the deferred decision |

**Note on PEP-723 header for `bin/executable_fleet`**: copy from `bin/executable_sms:1-10` style (`--quiet` flag included), not `scripts/fleet_apply.py:1-9` style — the binary should not log its own startup noise.

## Subcommand mapping

| `fleet <sub>` | Existing `just` recipe | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| `fleet apply [--hosts ...] [--dry-run] [--force] ...` | `fleet-apply`, `fleet-apply-dry-run`, `fleet-apply-one`, `fleet-diff`, `fleet-apply-file`, `fleet-apply-branch[-force]` | `scripts.fleet.apply.main` |
| `fleet status` (readiness, default) | `fleet-status` | `apply --readiness` path |
| `fleet status --quick` | `fleet-status-quick` | `apply --readiness --readiness-no-fetch` |
| `fleet status --live [--watch N]` | `fleet-apply-status`, `fleet-apply-watch` | `apply --status` path — overload disambiguated via `--live` |
| `fleet tail HOST[:RUN_ID]` | `fleet-apply-tail` | `apply --tail` |
| `fleet kill` | `fleet-apply-kill` | `apply --kill-orphans` |
| `fleet compact [--run-id ID]` | `fleet-apply-compact` | `apply --compact` |
| `fleet edit` | `fleet-edit` | New — port seed text from `justfile:471-476` |
| `fleet tmux ...` | — | new |
| `fleet info ...` | — | new |

**Flag pass-through**: keep tyro signatures from `scripts/fleet/apply.py` verbatim — `fleet apply --hosts X --dry-run --force ...` works identically to today's `./scripts/fleet_apply.py --hosts X --dry-run --force ...`.

## `fleet tmux` design

**CLI**:
\```
fleet tmux [--hosts X,Y] [--exclude Z] [--json] [--deep]
          [--connect-timeout N] [--serial] [--max-parallel N]
\```

`--with-summary` (LLM aggregate across hosts) → **out of scope this round**; stub raises `NotImplementedError` with a hint to use `tsum` locally.

**Upstream change in `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`** — minimal patch:
1. Add `p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit raw session/window JSON; skip LLM and cache.")` after L818.
2. After L829 (`sessions = collect_sessions(deep=args.deep)`), insert:
   \```python
   if args.json:
       import json as _json
       print(_json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(s) for s in sessions], default=str))
       return 0
   \```
3. Schema: `Session{name, created, attached, last_attached, windows[], active_pane_tail, active_pane_skipped}` × `Window{index, name, active, cwd, cmd, panes}` — direct `dataclasses.asdict()` of existing dataclasses (L208-227).
4. `--json` interaction: bypasses cache, bypasses LLM, ignores `--dry-run`/`--refresh`/`--no-cache`. `--deep` still controls pane capture.

**Remote dispatcher** (`scripts/fleet/tmux.py`):
\```bash
# Single ssh blob per host; tries preferred path then falls back.
set +e
if [ -x "$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py" ]; then
  out=$("$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py" --json ${DEEP_FLAG} 2>/dev/null)
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ -n "$out" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$out"; printf 'TSUM_SOURCE=py\n' >&2; exit 0
  fi
fi
# Fallback: raw tmux capture
printf 'TSUM_SOURCE=raw\n' >&2
tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}\t#{session_created}\t#{session_attached}\t#{session_last_attached}' 2>/dev/null
printf -- '---SEP---\n'
tmux list-windows -a -F '#{session_name}\t#{window_index}\t#{window_name}\t#{window_active}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{pane_current_command}\t#{window_panes}' 2>/dev/null
\```

Python parses the raw fallback back into the same `Session`/`Window` JSON schema, so downstream rendering is source-agnostic.

**Rich table columns**:
\```
HOST  SOURCE  SESSIONS  WINDOWS  ATTACHED  LAST_ATTACHED  TOP_SESSION
\```
- `SOURCE`: `py` / `raw` / `none` (when both paths empty) / `N/A` (host unreachable)
- `ATTACHED`: count of `session.attached == True`
- `LAST_ATTACHED`: max `last_attached` across sessions, humanized (`time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')`)
- `TOP_SESSION`: session with most windows; tie → most recently attached

**`--json`** emits per-host `{host, source, sessions: [...], error: null|str}` to stdout.

## `fleet info` design

**CLI**:
\```
fleet info [--hosts X] [--exclude Y] [--ff] [--full] [--modules cpu,mem,disk,...]
          [--json] [--verbose] [--connect-timeout N] [--serial] [--max-parallel N]
\```

**Default curated view**: `cpu, mem, disk, load, uptime, docker, chezmoi, os` (8 columns, render in <2s/host).

**Module catalog** (each entry: linux cmd + darwin cmd; runtime picks via `uname -s` in the SSH'd bash blob):

| Module | Linux | Darwin |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `awk -F: '/Model name/{print $2; exit}' /proc/cpuinfo; nproc` | `sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string; sysctl -n hw.ncpu` |
| `mem` | `awk '/MemTotal/{t=$2}/MemAvailable/{a=$2}END{print t-a, t}' /proc/meminfo` | `sysctl -n hw.memsize; vm_stat \| awk '...'` |
| `disk` | `df -PB1 / \| awk 'NR==2{print $3, $2}'` | same (POSIX) |
| `load` | `awk '{print $1, $2, $3}' /proc/loadavg` | `sysctl -n vm.loadavg \| tr -d '{}'` |
| `uptime` | `awk '{print int($1)}' /proc/uptime` | `echo $(( $(date +%s) - $(sysctl -n kern.boottime \| awk -F'[ ,]' '{print $4}') ))` |
| `docker` | `command -v docker >/dev/null && echo "$(docker ps -q \| wc -l) $(docker ps -aq \| wc -l)"` | same |
| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi --no-pager status 2>/dev/null \| wc -l; (cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && git rev-list --count HEAD..@{u} 2>/dev/null)` | same |
| `gpu` | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv,noheader,nounits 2>/dev/null` | `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json 2>/dev/null \| jq -r '...'` |
| `network` | `hostname -f; hostname -I \| awk '{print $1}'` | `hostname; ipconfig getifaddr en0 2>/dev/null \|\| ipconfig getifaddr en1` |
| `os` | `(lsb_release -ds 2>/dev/null) \|\| (. /etc/os-release && echo "$PRETTY_NAME")` | `echo "$(sw_vers -productName) $(sw_vers -productVersion)"` |

**Wire format**: one bash blob per host with `set +e`; each module emits `MOD_<name>=<value>` lines (or `MOD_<name>=ERR:<msg>`). Python parses key=value; missing key OR value starting with `ERR:` → render `"—"`; with `--verbose`, log the err to stderr.

**`--ff`**: invokes `fastfetch --format json` over SSH; if `command -v fastfetch` fails → row's `--ff` cell = `"—"`. Output: per-host flat key-value Rich table (or section-per-host with `--json` raw).

**`--full`**: enumerates every module from the catalog (default 8 + `gpu, network`).

**`--modules a,b,c`**: comma-split, intersect with catalog; warn on unknown.

**Failure policy**: per-host orchestration wrapped in `try/except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)`; host row reads `STATUS=N/A` and `error=<type>`; the run continues. Same pattern as `_run_kill` at `fleet_apply.py:1486-1508`.

**`--json` mode**: per-host `{host, status: "ok"|"N/A", modules: {cpu: {model, cores}, mem: {used_bytes, total_bytes}, ...}, error: null|str}`.

## `backlog/bin-migration.md` (one-shot draft)

\```markdown
# bin-migration: relocate ~/bin to a chezmoi-distinct path

**Status**: P? / deferred — `~/bin` works today; collision risk is theoretical, not observed.

**Problem**: `~/bin` is a common collision target — third-party installers (Anaconda, asdf, mise, custom build scripts) may drop binaries there or expect it as user-writable. chezmoi's ownership of `~/bin/sms`, `~/bin/mi-router`, `~/bin/x`, `~/bin/sesh-preview`, `~/bin/fleet` (post-2026-05) makes "where did this binary come from" harder than it could be.

## Options

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Stay at `~/bin/` | Zero migration cost; widely understood | Collision risk persists |
| `~/.dotfiles-bin/` | Prefix telegraphs origin; clean isolation | Non-standard XDG; needs PATH update + every doc change |
| `~/.local/share/chezmoi-bin/` | XDG-aligned ("data" under chezmoi) | `share/` for executables is unconventional; long path |

## Files affected (any migration)

- `bin/executable_sms` / `mi-router` / `x` / `sesh-preview` / `fleet` — rename source dir (`bin/` → e.g. `dot_dotfiles-bin/`)
- `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:23` — PATH export
- `justfile` — audit for `~/bin` hardcodes
- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, any doc mentioning `~/bin/<x>`
- `pitfalls/*.md` — audit before migrating
- `bootstrap.sh` if it mentions PATH

## Migration ordering (when revisited)

1. Add new path to PATH alongside old (so old `~/bin/sms` keeps working during transition)
2. `chezmoi apply` deploys to new path
3. Flip doc references
4. Wait one release cycle
5. Remove `~/bin/` entries

## Decision

Deferred until either (a) a real collision happens, or (b) `bin/` exceeds ~10 entries. Re-evaluate at that point.

## Related

- Original discussion: 2026-05-13 fleet-CLI session (user raised the rename while adding `bin/fleet`)
- Decision rationale: bin-migration risk (5 existing binaries + PATH + docs) is uncorrelated with the value of adding `fleet`; bundling would expand blast radius for no upside.
\```

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: `fleet` umbrella CLI — extend fleet system with `tmux` / `info` subcommands

## Context

The fleet system (`scripts/fleet_apply.py`) is mature for `chezmoi update --init` orchestration but exposes only `just fleet-*` recipes — which fail outside the chezmoi source dir tree. Two new ops needs:

1. **Cross-host tmux session visibility**: multiple remote machines accumulate stale tmux sessions; the local `tsum` is local-only and AI-driven. Want a quick "what's open where" summary across the fleet.
2. **Cross-host system status**: fastfetch is installed everywhere via the `devtools` ansible role but never queried in aggregate. Want CPU/RAM/disk/uptime/load/docker glance across hosts.

User-locked design choices (asked & answered before this plan):
- **`~/bin/` stays** — bin/ relocation deferred to `backlog/bin-migration.md`
- **Umbrella `fleet` binary** with subcommands (`fleet apply / status / tmux / info / edit / tail / kill / compact`), matches `git`/`gh`/`chezmoi` pattern
- **Remote tmux**: prefer deployed `~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py --json`, fallback to raw `tmux list-sessions -F …` when missing/broken
- **`fleet info`**: default curated quick view; `--ff` runs fastfetch JSON dump; `--full` runs all built-in modules; `--modules a,b,c` lets user select; per-module fallback → render `"—"` instead of failing the host

## Architecture

```
bin/executable_fleet              ← new umbrella, uv-script
  → discovers chezmoi source-path
  → sys.path.insert + dispatches to scripts.fleet.<sub>.cli

scripts/fleet/                    ← new package
  __init__.py                     (empty marker)
  _lib.py                         (Host, load_hosts, _connect_kwargs,
                                   resolve_passwords, run_fanout,
                                   REMOTE_*/LOCAL_LOG_DIR constants)
  apply.py                        (lifted from current fleet_apply.py)
  tmux.py                         (new)
  info.py                         (new)

scripts/fleet_apply.py            ← becomes 10-line shim
                                   (preserves `./scripts/fleet_apply.py` callers)
```

**Why this shape**: shared inventory loading + asyncssh fan-out + Rich rendering belongs in one place (`_lib.py`); each subcommand keeps its orchestration logic in its own file. Avoids re-importing dataclasses from a `fleet_apply.py` filename that no longer describes the scope.

**Why an umbrella binary (not separate `fleet-tmux`/`fleet-info`)**: tyro supports `subcommand_cli_from_dict` natively; single PATH entry; consistent `fleet --help` discoverability; bin/ stays small.

**Backward compat**: `scripts/fleet_apply.py` keeps its current shebang + PEP-723 header; body becomes `from scripts.fleet.apply import main; sys.exit(main())`. Every `just fleet-*` recipe continues to call `./scripts/fleet_apply.py …` unchanged during the transition. Justfile recipes get rewritten as `fleet <sub>` wrappers AFTER the binary is smoked.

## Files (new / modified)

| File | Change | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/executable_fleet` (NEW) | uv-script (`#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script`, PEP-723 deps: `asyncssh>=2.18, tyro>=0.9, rich>=13.9`); locates `chezmoi source-path`, dispatches to `scripts.fleet.*.cli` | Single binary, PATH-discoverable from anywhere |
| `scripts/fleet/__init__.py` (NEW) | Empty package marker | Make `scripts.fleet` importable |
| `scripts/fleet/_lib.py` (NEW) | `Host` (from `fleet_apply.py:62-89`), `load_hosts` (L101-157), `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` (L95), `_connect_kwargs` (L556-577), `resolve_passwords` (L191+), `LOCAL_LOG_DIR`/`REMOTE_*` constants (L243-252), generic `async def run_fanout(hosts, per_host_coro, *, parallelism, serial, console)` carved from `_run()` (L2971-3058) | DRY across apply/tmux/info subcommands |
| `scripts/fleet/apply.py` (NEW) | Current `cli()` body + all `_run_*` helpers + `build_remote_command` + `_classify_drift`; entrypoint `def main()` | Existing logic, just relocated |
| `scripts/fleet/tmux.py` (NEW) | `cli()` for `fleet tmux`, remote dispatcher (preferred `.py --json` + raw fallback), Rich table | See § fleet tmux |
| `scripts/fleet/info.py` (NEW) | `cli()` for `fleet info`, module catalog with linux/darwin dispatch, fastfetch path, per-module fallback | See § fleet info |
| `scripts/fleet_apply.py` (MODIFY) | Body → `from scripts.fleet.apply import main; sys.exit(main())`. Keep shebang + PEP-723 header. | Backward compat for `just fleet-*` recipes |
| `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py` (MODIFY) | Insert `--json` flag in `parse_args` (after L818); short-circuit at L829 after `collect_sessions(deep=args.deep)`: `if args.json: print(json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(s) for s in sessions], default=str)); return 0` | Reuse existing dataclasses, avoid LLM call when fleet just needs raw data |
| `justfile` (MODIFY) | Add `fleet *ARGS: fleet {{ARGS}}` recipe. Leave the 14 existing `fleet-*` recipes as-is for now (they still call `./scripts/fleet_apply.py` which is now a shim). Optionally add `fleet-tmux` / `fleet-info` wrappers for parity. | Muscle memory + new helpers both available |
| `CLAUDE.md` (MODIFY) | Update the cross-file maintenance row at L7-19 from `scripts/fleet_apply.py / justfile fleet-*…` to `bin/executable_fleet / scripts/fleet/ / justfile fleet-*…`. Still points at `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`. | Track new surface |
| `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` (MODIFY) | New sections: `## Umbrella binary` (path discovery, `fleet --help` overview), `## fleet tmux`, `## fleet info`. Document `fleet status` overload (readiness default vs `--live` for process probe). | Single doc anchor for the whole fleet surface |
| `backlog/bin-migration.md` (NEW) | One-shot draft (see § backlog content) | Per project-knowledge-harness convention; captures the deferred decision |

**Note on PEP-723 header for `bin/executable_fleet`**: copy from `bin/executable_sms:1-10` style (`--quiet` flag included), not `scripts/fleet_apply.py:1-9` style — the binary should not log its own startup noise.

## Subcommand mapping

| `fleet <sub>` | Existing `just` recipe | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| `fleet apply [--hosts ...] [--dry-run] [--force] ...` | `fleet-apply`, `fleet-apply-dry-run`, `fleet-apply-one`, `fleet-diff`, `fleet-apply-file`, `fleet-apply-branch[-force]` | `scripts.fleet.apply.main` |
| `fleet status` (readiness, default) | `fleet-status` | `apply --readiness` path |
| `fleet status --quick` | `fleet-status-quick` | `apply --readiness --readiness-no-fetch` |
| `fleet status --live [--watch N]` | `fleet-apply-status`, `fleet-apply-watch` | `apply --status` path — overload disambiguated via `--live` |
| `fleet tail HOST[:RUN_ID]` | `fleet-apply-tail` | `apply --tail` |
| `fleet kill` | `fleet-apply-kill` | `apply --kill-orphans` |
| `fleet compact [--run-id ID]` | `fleet-apply-compact` | `apply --compact` |
| `fleet edit` | `fleet-edit` | New — port seed text from `justfile:471-476` |
| `fleet tmux ...` | — | new |
| `fleet info ...` | — | new |

**Flag pass-through**: keep tyro signatures from `scripts/fleet/apply.py` verbatim — `fleet apply --hosts X --dry-run --force ...` works identically to today's `./scripts/fleet_apply.py --hosts X --dry-run --force ...`.

## `fleet tmux` design

**CLI**:
```
fleet tmux [--hosts X,Y] [--exclude Z] [--json] [--deep]
          [--connect-timeout N] [--serial] [--max-parallel N]
```

`--with-summary` (LLM aggregate across hosts) → **out of scope this round**; stub raises `NotImplementedError` with a hint to use `tsum` locally.

**Upstream change in `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`** — minimal patch:
1. Add `p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit raw session/window JSON; skip LLM and cache.")` after L818.
2. After L829 (`sessions = collect_sessions(deep=args.deep)`), insert:
   ```python
   if args.json:
       import json as _json
       print(_json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(s) for s in sessions], default=str))
       return 0
   ```
3. Schema: `Session{name, created, attached, last_attached, windows[], active_pane_tail, active_pane_skipped}` × `Window{index, name, active, cwd, cmd, panes}` — direct `dataclasses.asdict()` of existing dataclasses (L208-227).
4. `--json` interaction: bypasses cache, bypasses LLM, ignores `--dry-run`/`--refresh`/`--no-cache`. `--deep` still controls pane capture.

**Remote dispatcher** (`scripts/fleet/tmux.py`):
```bash
# Single ssh blob per host; tries preferred path then falls back.
set +e
if [ -x "$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py" ]; then
  out=$("$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py" --json ${DEEP_FLAG} 2>/dev/null)
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ -n "$out" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$out"; printf 'TSUM_SOURCE=py\n' >&2; exit 0
  fi
fi
# Fallback: raw tmux capture
printf 'TSUM_SOURCE=raw\n' >&2
tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_name}\t#{session_created}\t#{session_attached}\t#{session_last_attached}' 2>/dev/null
printf -- '---SEP---\n'
tmux list-windows -a -F '#{session_name}\t#{window_index}\t#{window_name}\t#{window_active}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{pane_current_command}\t#{window_panes}' 2>/dev/null
```

Python parses the raw fallback back into the same `Session`/`Window` JSON schema, so downstream rendering is source-agnostic.

**Rich table columns**:
```
HOST  SOURCE  SESSIONS  WINDOWS  ATTACHED  LAST_ATTACHED  TOP_SESSION
```
- `SOURCE`: `py` / `raw` / `none` (when both paths empty) / `N/A` (host unreachable)
- `ATTACHED`: count of `session.attached == True`
- `LAST_ATTACHED`: max `last_attached` across sessions, humanized (`time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')`)
- `TOP_SESSION`: session with most windows; tie → most recently attached

**`--json`** emits per-host `{host, source, sessions: [...], error: null|str}` to stdout.

**`--full`**: enumerates every module from the catalog (default 8 + `gpu, network`).

**`--modules a,b,c`**: comma-split, intersect with catalog; warn on unknown.

**Failure policy**: per-host orchestration wrapped in `try/except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, TimeoutError)`; host row reads `STATUS=N/A` and `error=<type>`; the run continues. Same pattern as `_run_kill` at `fleet_apply.py:1486-1508`.

**`--json` mode**: per-host `{host, status: "ok"|"N/A", modules: {cpu: {model, cores}, mem: {used_bytes, total_bytes}, ...}, error: null|str}`.

## `backlog/bin-migration.md` (one-shot draft)

```markdown
# bin-migration: relocate ~/bin to a chezmoi-distinct path

**Status**: P? / deferred — `~/bin` works today; collision risk is theoretical, not observed.

**Problem**: `~/bin` is a common collision target — third-party installers (Anaconda, asdf, mise, custom build scripts) may drop binaries there or expect it as user-writable. chezmoi's ownership of `~/bin/sms`, `~/bin/mi-router`, `~/bin/x`, `~/bin/sesh-preview`, `~/bin/fleet` (post-2026-05) makes "where did this binary come from" harder than it could be.

## Options

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Stay at `~/bin/` | Zero migration cost; widely understood | Collision risk persists |
| `~/.dotfiles-bin/` | Prefix telegraphs origin; clean isolation | Non-standard XDG; needs PATH update + every doc change |
| `~/.local/share/chezmoi-bin/` | XDG-aligned ("data" under chezmoi) | `share/` for executables is unconventional; long path |

## Files affected (any migration)

- `bin/executable_sms` / `mi-router` / `x` / `sesh-preview` / `fleet` — rename source dir (`bin/` → e.g. `dot_dotfiles-bin/`)
- `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:23` — PATH export
- `justfile` — audit for `~/bin` hardcodes
- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, any doc mentioning `~/bin/<x>`
- `pitfalls/*.md` — audit before migrating
- `bootstrap.sh` if it mentions PATH

## Migration ordering (when revisited)

1. Add new path to PATH alongside old (so old `~/bin/sms` keeps working during transition)
2. `chezmoi apply` deploys to new path
3. Flip doc references
4. Wait one release cycle
5. Remove `~/bin/` entries

## Decision

Deferred until either (a) a real collision happens, or (b) `bin/` exceeds ~10 entries. Re-evaluate at that point.

## Related

- Original discussion: 2026-05-13 fleet-CLI session (user raised the rename while adding `bin/fleet`)
- Decision rationale: bin-migration risk (5 existing binaries + PATH + docs) is uncorrelated with the value of adding `fleet`; bundling would expand blast radius for no upside.
```

End-to-end (in order):

1. `fleet apply --hosts self --dry-run` — confirms shim + tyro umbrella works locally
2. `just fleet-apply --hosts self --dry-run` — confirms existing recipe still works (regression)
3. `fleet status` (readiness) + `fleet status --live` — overload disambiguation works
4. `fleet tmux --hosts self` — preferred `.py --json` path; local tmux server populated
5. `fleet tmux --hosts <remote-with-tmux>` — remote `.py --json` path
6. `fleet tmux --hosts <remote-no-py>` — fallback raw path engages (verify `SOURCE=raw` in table)
7. `fleet tmux --hosts <remote-no-tmux-server>` — empty session list, row shows `0` not `N/A`
8. `fleet tmux --hosts <unreachable>` — row `N/A`, run continues (per-host failure isolation)
9. `fleet info` (default 8 modules)
10. `fleet info --ff` — fastfetch JSON dump
11. `fleet info --full --hosts <no-gpu-host>` — `gpu` cell renders `"—"`, others populated
12. `fleet info --modules cpu,mem` — filtered output
13. `fleet info --hosts <no-docker>` — `docker` cell `"—"`, others populated
14. `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py --json` locally — schema matches what `fleet tmux` parser expects (no AI agent invoked)
15. Concurrent: `fleet apply --hosts X` + `fleet info --hosts X` — no shared-state collision (info is read-only, doesn't touch `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/`)

Edge cases to specifically exercise:
- SSH `connect_timeout` exceeded → `asyncssh.ConnectionLost` → row `N/A`
- Host with `python3` missing (rare; older BSD/CentOS) → preferred `tmux` path fails; fallback works
- Host with mismatched `tmux` binary on PATH (apt 3.2 vs ~/.local/bin/tmux 3.5) → fallback uses whatever `tmux` resolves on remote PATH (same TSUM_TMUX_BIN caveat as today's `tsum`)

561	    IdentityFile/ProxyJump from ssh_config. Explicit fields override.

564	    assert target is not None  # validated in load_hosts
565	    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
566	    # known_hosts=None tells asyncssh to skip its own check; we still rely on
567	    # the user having ssh'd manually first (StrictHostKeyChecking is enforced
568	    # implicitly by them adding it to ~/.ssh/known_hosts ahead of time).
569	    # Switching to known_hosts=() would force strict but reject every new host.
570	    if host.user:

572	    if host.port:
573	        kwargs["port"] = host.port
574	    if host.identity_file:
575	        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
